LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Denver is coming off a lackluster win vs. the Chargers, while Seattle looks to rebound after falling to the 49ers Getty Images In the Week 6 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Denver Broncos play host to the Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos are coming off their third win in the last four games, though it required a late, game-winning drive against the decrepit division rival Los Angeles Chargers . The return of Sean Payton as play-caller didn't exactly result in an explosive or efficient offense, but the Broncos did just enough to hold off L.A. and climb back over .500. The Seahawks, meanwhile, dropped to 3-2 after falling to their own division rivals in the San Francisco 49ers . The Niners moved the ball quite well against the vaunted Seattle defense, and turnovers in their own territory haunted the Seahawks and ultimately cost them the game. Will the Seahawks bounce back, or will the Broncos capture their second consecutive victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Broncos vs. Seahawks live Date: Thursday, Oct. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Empower Field at Mile High (Denver) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Seahawks have the ball Let's start here: the Seahawks cannot run the ball at all. They couldn't run the ball when rookie running back Jadarian Price was healthy earlier in the season, and they haven't been able to run the ball since he's been out. The trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has combined for just 447 yards on 127 carries -- an average of just 3.5 per tote. The Seahawks do not get much push up front, as their backs average a mere 0.69 yards before contact per carry, a figure that ranks fourth-worst in the NFL , according to Tru Media. Their 2.83 yards after contact per carry is more respectable, ranking 14th league-wide. The Broncos will have to be careful there. They've allowed the third-fewest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league so far (0.59), but the most rushing yards after contact (3.92), thanks to a sky-high avoided tackle rate by enemy backs (30.1%). Much of that production came from Kenneth Walker III in the season opener, but even in Weeks 2 through 5, the Broncos rank in the bottom third of the league in both yards after contact per attempt and broken tackle rate. Wilson is likely to be the primary runner once again while Price and Zach Charbonnet remain sidelined. The Broncos will have to get him on the ground on the first try, limiting the yards he can gain after contact, because the Seahawks just don't create much for him in the first place. He scarcely gets more than is blocked without breaking through tackles. In the passing game, Sam Darnold has struggled to replicate last year's results -- especially over the last two weeks. In games against the Chargers and 49ers, Darnold went just 31-of-51 for 363 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. After leading the league in turnovers last season, Darnold has already been picked off five times in his three full appearances this season, while his yards per attempt average is down from 8.5 to just 7.7. His completion rate is down over 3 percentage points as well. Denver's pass defense has been largely good so far this year, with the Broncos ranking fifth in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media. The Broncos just held the Chargers to 82 net passing yards last week, which plays a huge role in that figure, but they've also allowed only one team ( Rams ) to top 218 net passing yards in any game so far. (The Chiefs didn't have to throw the ball very much in Week 1, though, because they did whatever they wanted on the ground.) The Broncos won't have Patrick Surtain II or Talanoa Hufanga here, and Riley Moss is listed as questionable -- all of which is a significant issue when you're going up against Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who leads the NFL in both receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine figure to see increased roles due to the cornerback injuries, while Devon Key will play more in the wake of Hufanga's absence. They'll all have their work cut out for them against JSN. The Seahawks really don't throw the ball to anyone else all that often. When the Broncos have the ball Denver might have gotten a win last week, but Sean Payton's return as play-caller didn't have much to do with it. The Broncos entered the game against the Chargers averaging a miserable 4.9 yards per play, then averaged a mere 3.9 per play in the win over Los Angeles. Bo Nix totaled just 123 yards on his 27 pass attempts, J.K. Dobbins ran for only 68 yards on his 18 carries, Jaylen Waddle caught just two of five balls thrown his way for just 19 yards ... nothing went well offensively. And nothing has gone right pretty much all year, with the exception of the second halves of the Broncos' wins over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3. Two good halves in five weeks isn't much to write home about, even if those halves helped the Broncos steal a pair of wins and arrive at 3-2. Nix is essentially refusing to push the ball down the field so far this season. His average air yards per attempt in each of his first two years of his career was 7.3, according to Tru Media, but that figure has dropped all the way to 5.2 this year. He threw deep on 13.1% of his passes as a rookie and 11.8% of them last year, but he's done so on only 7.4% of his attempts this season. Nix also isn't running anymore. He scrambled 27.3% of the time when pressured during his rookie season and 16.1% of the time last season. That number is all the way down to 5.6% so far this year, meaning he's scrambled only four times in five games. All of this, combined with his insistence on checking down repeatedly, has made the pass offense feel neutered to date. Meanwhile, the Broncos also can't run the ball. Dobbins looks like he's running with a piano on his back, slogging his way to 3.6 yards per carry. RJ Harvey barely gets opportunities, but he hasn't done any better at only 3.7 yards per carry. Harvey is at least productive in the short passing game, but the Broncos de-emphasized that last week under Payton in favor of more Dobbins runs that went nowhere. The Seahawks have largely been their usual selves defensively through the first five weeks of the season. They've arrived at their two losses largely by virtue of their offense repeatedly turning the ball over against the Commanders (three times) and 49ers (four, including a fumble that resulted in a touchdown). Seattle has held opponents to the fewest passing yards in the league and the fewest net yards per attempt, and it has limited running games to the eighth-fewest yards per attempt as well. It's hard to see the Broncos snapping out of their funk against this unit. Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have let the Broncos come away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Surtain here, which is obviously a problem against JSN. away.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks suffered a tough loss on Sunday in NFL Week 5, and now they have more difficult news: Zach Charbonnet is not expected to return in Week 6 when the team plays on Thursday night. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said the plan is for Charbonnet to remain out as he continues recovering from a knee injury. He returned to practice ahead of Week 4 after beginning the season on the physically unable to perform list, but the short turnaround following Sunday's game makes Thursday's return unrealistic. That is not an ideal situation heading into a matchup with the Broncos. Denver has built one of the NFL's more difficult defensive units, and Seattle will need to find ways to move the football without the experienced Charbonnet available. It is impossible to know whether Charbonnet would have prevented that specific mistake, but there is no question Seattle would have been in a better position with one of its more experienced backs available. Holani's fumble was one of several costly mistakes that ultimately contributed to Seattle's three-point loss. Now the Seahawks have to move forward without Charbonnet for at least one more game. Seattle will face Denver on Thursday before getting additional time to prepare for Week 7, which currently looks like a more realistic target for Charbonnet's return. home.headline: Final Seahawks, Broncos Injury Report Clarifies Situation On Both Sides
home.blurb: It's time for the third and final practice report of this week, this one coming complete with game statuses for players who missed some (or all) of potential practice time this week . The Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos are both staring down the barrel of a short week, so who are they going to have available? Let's have a look at it. Moving past the long-term, ongoing injuries to players like Jadarian Price, Anthony Bradford, and Zach Charbonnet (knee, still out), it's not too bad. Chazz Surratt (calf) is out, a pure special teamer. The main concern is Drake Thomas (ankle), who did not practice and is out for tomorrow . The team will turn to Tyrice Knight in his absence, which isn't entirely a bad thing, but still a step down. That's about it. No one else was listed as questionable. Beau Stephens (shoulder) and George Holani (ribs, knee) held as full participants and are ready to roll. Irv Charles (knee) was removed from the report entirely due to being put down on the practice squad in a roster switcharoo with Velus Jones Jr, but should be available for an elevation tomorrow to get his Seattle debut. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) was listed as a full participant today, which should make people feel better about things after his (hypothetical) limited days the last two practices. Drew Lock (right forearm) and much more importantly Leonard Williams (ankle) have no game status despite limited participation today and should be available in full as needed Thursday night. If the Seahawks can not find a way to throw the ball effectively against the Broncos in their current state of health, then there may not be much hope for them. As anticipated throughout the week, Patrick Surtain (ankle) and Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) are both out. That's Denver's best CB (and one of the best in the league) and best safety unavailable. And the bad news doesn't stop there either. Riley Moss (ribs) is questionable, indicative of the fact that while he's more likely than not to play, he's clearly not himself. Denver is highly motivated to toss him onto the field no matter what due to how helpless they'd be at boundary cornerback without him, but that doesn't mean he's in good shape to go. The Jags are playing their second consecutive international games, both taking place in London. They defeated the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last week. The last-second win put them at 4-1 on the season, tied for the second-best record in the AFC. The Texans come in with a bit different standing, sitting at 1-4, though, like the Jags, they are also coming off a win. Houston got their first win against the Tennessee Titans , who now sit at 0-5. Texans vs. Jaguars need to know Jaguars London history: The Jags are pretty much London's home team, playing there at least once a year since 2013, with the exception of 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic, with an 8-7 record across the pond. Their first-ever game in England was in 2013, a loss to the 49ers at Wembley Stadium. Their first international win was their third of the kind, a 2015 game against the Bills . And of course, their most recent win came in Week 5 against the Eagles. Marvin Harrison Jr. : The biggest news out of Houston is the addition of former No. 4 overall pick Marvin Harrison Jr. joining the team. Harrison's time with the Arizona Cardinals didn't work out as expected, but he and the Texans are hoping a fresh start will be reflected in his stat line. What should help the WR make a quick adjustment to his new team is the reunion with quarterback C.J. Stroud , who he had great success with at Ohio State. Harrison will be one to watch this week as the Texans offense has the tall task of keeping up with a solid Jaguars offense. Stroud has played well despite their record, so adding Harrison could be huge for the Texans' offense. Jaguars o-line vs. Texans defense: The Jags will be without left tackle Anton Harrison , who needs surgery. The offensive line will be going up against defensive end Will Anderson Jr. , who has 27 total tackles, 7.5 sacks, a league high, and one forced fumble and recovery this season. The Jags need to protect Trevor Lawrence, especially so he can continue to improve in his game-time decisions. Meanwhile, the Jaguars are eyeing the No. 1 seed in the AFC and have been an elite offensive team (sixth in EPA/Play) through their first five games. Yet, oddsmakers have set a relatively low total (42.5) after the Jaguars combined for just 36 points in their first London game this season against Philly. The Texans haven’t had a ton of playmakers this season, and it’s worth noting that Jacksonville gave up a rushing score to Eagles starter Will Shipley in Week 5. Parker Washington Anytime TD (+180) Jaguars star receiver Parker Washington has found the end zone in three of his five games this season, hitting paydirt four times in total. Not only that, but Washington has made some ridiculous grabs – including his touchdown in Week 5 – to bail out Trevor Lawrence. Jacksonville’s passing offense hits a ton of big plays and ranks No. 3 in the NFL in EPA/Pass. I love this price for Washington (nearly 2/1) since no other Jags receiver has been a consistent threat to lead the team in targets. Nico Collins Anytime TD (+165) Texans No. 1 receiver Nico Collins has found the end zone in two of his three appearances this season, catching three scores overall. Jacksonville has also given up the third-most passing yards in the NFL and ranks outside the top-20 in the league in yards per play allowed. David Montgomery, Jalen Pitre Out as Expected Two of the non-participants from the Texans' Wednesday practice were to be expected: that's running back David Montgomery, who's dealing with a groin injury, as well as defensive back Jalen Pitre, who suffered an AC joint sprain during last weekend's game against the Tennessee Titans. As of now, their status is considered week-to-week, meaning there's a good chance that both could be sidelined for Week 6 against the Jaguars, yet might not have to be forced on injured reserve, which would take them out for a minimum of four weeks. The two other DNPs from the Texans' practice- linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair and Trent Brown- have both been dealing with some nagging injuries through the past couple of weeks that effectively left them to sit out of Wednesday's practice. However, considering both played in last week's game against the Titans while dealing with their respective injuries, it'd be fair to assume that both are still on track to play in Week 6 against the Jaguars. Henry To'oTo'o Trending Up for Return The Texans officially activated the 21-day return window for Henry To'oTo'o on Wednesday, who's been sidelined for the past four weeks due to a shoulder injury he suffered in Week 1 against the Buffalo Bills. A limited participation in practice is a great sign that his return is right around the corner. However, he might still be ruled inactive for Week 6 against the Jaguars if unable to complete a full practice. If that's the case, Jake Hansen will remain Houston's fill in as their WLB. Another aspect of the Texans' injury report that can't go unnoticed: wide receiver Tank Dell has participated in his first full practice since being designated to return from his knee injury suffered back in 2024. That means, if all goes smoothly over the coming days, there's a chance that Dell could make his long-awaited return to the lineup in Week 6. But until the Texans officially activate him from injured reserve , we won't know for sure about when he'll officially be good to be elevated on the gameday roster. away.headline: Report: Bears QB Caleb Williams to start vs. Falcons
away.blurb: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is expected to return to the starting lineup Sunday against the Falcons in Atlanta after missing the previous three games with a hamstring injury, ESPN and NFL Network reported Saturday. The Bears officially listed Williams as questionable Friday, but he handled first-team work and continued to progress through the final two practices of the week, according to the reports. His return sets up the first NFL meeting between Williams and Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr., two of the six quarterbacks selected in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft. Chicago took Williams first overall, while the Falcons selected Penix at No. 8. Williams, who has been sidelined since injuring his right hamstring against the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 20, practiced fully throughout the week without a setback. Coach Ben Johnson said Friday that Williams was "on track" after the quarterback increased his workload. Chicago went 2-1 without Williams. Case Keenum started a Week 3 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles before Tyson Bagent led the Bears past the New York Jets in Week 4 and started last week's loss to the Green Bay Packers. Williams has completed 36 of 55 passes for 407 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in two games this season. He also has rushed for 107 yards and two scores. The injury ended a run of 36 consecutive regular-season starts for Williams dating to the beginning of his NFL career. Penix also dealt with an injury this week after hurting his ribs in Atlanta's Week 5 loss to Baltimore. The Bears (3-2) will try to rebound from their loss at Green Bay against the Falcons (2-3). away.headline: Chicago Bears DE Montez Sweat suspended for violating NFL performance-enhancing substances policy
away.blurb: Updated on: October 13, 2026 / 3:19 PM CDT / CBS Chicago Chicago Bears defensive end Montez Sweat is suspended for the team's next two games without pay for violating the NFL's performance-enhancing substances policy, the NFL said Tuesday. The NFL did not specify further details about what Sweat is accused of doing or what kind of drugs he is accused of taking. This means Sweat will not play with the Bears when they take on the Atlanta Falcons this coming Sunday, nor when they take on the New England Patriots on Thursday of next week. He will be eligible for reinstatement on Friday, Oct. 23, after the Bears-Patriots game. In the next game after that, the Bears take on the Seattle Seahawks. The Bears acquired the rusher Sweat from the Washington Commanders in the fall of 2023.

Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. away.headline: Major injury update for Lamar Jackson and the Ravens
away.blurb: According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, Jackson could be available for Sunday’s AFC North matchup against the Cleveland Browns, providing an encouraging development for a Ravens team looking to maintain its early-season momentum. “Ravens QB Lamar Jackson has a realistic chance to return for Sunday’s game at Cleveland, per league source,” Schefter reported Wednesday. The update comes after Jackson suffered an ankle injury during Baltimore’s Week 4 victory over the Tennessee Titans. Jackson exited the game at halftime and did not return, leaving backup quarterback Tyler Huntley to finish the contest. The Ravens held on for a 24-18 victory, but Jackson’s injury immediately raised concerns about how long Baltimore might be without its two-time NFL MVP. Those concerns increased when Jackson missed practice the following week and was eventually ruled out against Atlanta. However, the latest report suggests his absence could be limited to just one game. “To Lamar’s credit, he’s doing everything he can to get back out there,” Minter added. “I think we’ll know more by the middle of the week.” Jackson’s potential return would be significant for a Baltimore offense that has relied heavily on his ability to create plays through the air and on the ground. Through four appearances this season, Jackson has completed 70.8% of his passes for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception. Although the Ravens would welcome his return, Huntley has helped keep the team moving in his absence. His participation in practice and how his ankle responds throughout the week will likely play an important role in determining whether he can return against Cleveland. The Baltimore Ravens could be getting their starting quarterback back sooner than expected. After missing Baltimore’s Week 5 victory over the Atlanta Falcons with an ankle injury, Lamar Jackson reportedly has a realistic chance of returning to the field this weekend. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter had already offered an encouraging update Monday, explaining that Jackson was making progress in his recovery. “He’s definitely doing better,” Minter said . Minter also acknowledged that the team was still evaluating whether Jackson would be ready to participate in practice Wednesday. He has also contributed 144 rushing yards and another touchdown, continuing to provide the dual-threat production that makes him one of the NFL’s most difficult quarterbacks to defend. The veteran quarterback stepped into the starting role against Atlanta and delivered a strong performance in Baltimore’s 30-23 overtime victory. Huntley completed 24 of 32 passes for 201 yards and two touchdowns, helping the Ravens overcome a difficult road challenge. He also played an important role in the closing moments, leading a game-tying touchdown drive late in regulation before scoring the winning touchdown on a quarterback sneak in overtime. away.headline: The Ravens Inactives For Week 6 With Lamar Jackson Out
away.blurb: The Ravens Inactives For Week 6 With Lamar Jackson Out Skip to main content SI.COM The Ravens ruled out two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson (ankle) on Friday yet again but still faced numerous critical medical decision to make before Sunday’s kickoff in Cleveland. Rookie coach Jesse Minter is facing his first AFC North opponent with an injury report that stretched to 19 names midweek. Baltimore ruled out Jackson, center Cam Jurgens (concussion), defensive lineman Broderick Washington (ankle) and rookie tight end Matthew Hibner (hand). The team has had to juggle its offensive line every week all season, Jurgens has not appeared in two games since general manager Eric DeCosta made a desperate move to land him and Baltimore was once again dealing with injuries to guards as well, with John Simpson playing through a groin problem and Andrew Vorhees (foot) and Emery Jones (ankle) both listed as questionable. And the Ravens had to decide if third-round pick Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) was healthy and conditioned enough to play his first game since Week 1, when the promising youngster suffered an injury in the first half and has not played since. Lane was one of the stories of the summer and the preseason and quickly worked himself into a starting role with the team, and with Baltimore dealing with injuries at tight end and with $13M “move” tight end Mark Andrews struggling mightily , having a big receiver (6-foot-4) available for backup quarterback Snoop Huntley is a big deal. Undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano was once again active and serving as the primary backup to Huntley. The Ravens are hopeful that Jackson, who has yet to take the practice field since suffering the ankle injury just before halftime in Week 4, can return to practice this week with the Bengals traveling to Baltimore in Week 7, with Minter continuing to refer to him as “day-to-day” this week and Jurgens should also be cleared to begin practicing fully next week barring any setbacks with his return from concussion protocol. Lane was cleared to play for the first time since Week 1, while Vorhees was not. The Ravens welcomed back $30M edge rusher Trey Hendrickson after a two-week absence due to a procedure on his finger. They are as healthy as they have been all season up front on defense – Washington is a rotational run stuffer at this point – all season. The defense in particular has been in better health than the offensive side of the ball, yet the offense has carried the team to the 4-1 start. away.blurb: Ravens Final Week 6 Injury Report: Four Players Ruled Out - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Ravens Final Week 6 Injury Report: Four Players Ruled Out While it had been established that the Ravens would likely be without quarterback Lamar Jackson for another game, he has officially been ruled out, along with three others. Center Cam Jurgens also remains out as he works his way back from concussion protocol. The Ravens traded for the former Philadelphia Eagles center before Week 5, but he was in the protocol when the trade took place. With Jurgens out, this means rookie guard Vega Ioane will step in as the center yet again. Additionally, guard Andrew Vorhees is questionable with a foot injury, and he may need more time to heal as well. Emery Jones Jr. may get the start on Sunday, especially so as not to lead to a further injury for Vorhees. The issue is that Jones is also questionable, pointing to what could be an issue if both are not able to play. Finally, defensive tackle Broderick Washington is out due to an ankle injury that he sustained in Week 5. Despite a full week of practice as a full participant, rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane is also questionable. He may not be ready to play, as he is still being designated to return from IR. No other players have injury statuses for the game. Despite the laundry list of injuries reported, the Ravens will have most of their key players available. Two concerns arose on Thursday when wide receiver Zay Flowers appeared on the injury report with a toe ailment, and linebacker Mike Green joined him with a hamstring. Both were limited and were upgraded to full participants on Friday. Outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson is also making his return after undergoing a procedure to fix his broken finger. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter spoke about the defender, saying he is excited to get him back out on the field. away.blurb: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Jackson's status Friday, ruling him out for the matchup. ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that Jackson had a "realistic chance to return for Sunday's game," with Minter telling reporters that Jackson was considered day-to-day. Minter added that Jackson is "working his butt off" and "doing everything he can" to return to the field. Jackson was out for Week 5 as Tyler Huntley led the Ravens to an overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns as he continues to recover from an ankle injury. He initially left Week 4's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury and didn't play in the second half, a concerning development for a Ravens' offense very much reliant on the dynamic quarterback's unique skill set. While the Ravens didn't believe at the time that Jackson's injury was going to be a long-term issue, there was uncertainty over his short-term availability. "I really don't think it's going to be crazy long term, but we'll see what happens," head coach Jesse Minter told reporters at the time. There's no replacing a two-time MVP and three-time first-team All-Pro like Jackson, though the Ravens do have an experienced backup in Huntley. "There's one Lamar Jackson, the guy's a two-time MVP," Minter said after Week 4. "And so I think for anybody to have to say we're being compared to Lamar is unfair and not realistic. I think [Huntley] as a backup quarterback in this league and even as a starter at times has shown the ability to come in and really kind of run the offense, make plays with his legs, be able to make plays on third down." Injuries were also a concern for Jackson last season, as he missed four games due to a hamstring injury and a back contusion. Huntley started two of those games, leading the team to a 2-0 record. Browns RB1 a true game-time call After missing Cleveland's first two practices this week, Judkins returned as a limited participant on Friday, giving some hope that he might be able to push through his ankle issue against Baltimore. But on Sunday morning, Ian Rapoport poured some cold water on that optimism: It sounds like Judkins is a true game-time decision, with pregame workouts determining whether he'll be able to go. Dylan Sampson has already been ruled out for Week 6 as he ramps up after starting the season on injured reserve, and Raheim Sanders just got put on IR himself earlier in the week. The Browns picked up Audric Estime off the Vikings' practice squad, but as things stand, he and Jaleel McLaughlin are the only two running backs we can say with certainty will enter Sunday's game at something close to full health. Of the other two available options, McLaughlin would seem to be the preferable play from a fantasy perspective. He's more of a receiving back than the bruising Estime, but he's also been with the Browns all season, whereas Estime is just now getting up to speed with a new team. He's rarely shouldered double-digit carries at the NFL level, but he flashed some real versatility across three seasons with the Broncos before coming to Cleveland in 2026. Of course, if you want to steer clear of this backfield entirely, that's more than understandable given the uncertainty and the tough matchup. Some other viable flex options include Dameon Pierce, who's filling in for the injured Saquon Barkley in a beleaguered Eagles backfield on Sunday, and iffier options like Bears RB Roschon Johnson (filling in for an injured Kyle Monangai) and Patriots RB Corey Kiner (with TreVeyon Henderson out). Is Caleb Williams playing today? Bears Week 6 injury as QB eyes return Sunday's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens is the biggest game the Cleveland Browns have had in recent memory, with a chance to move to 4-2 and assume first place in the AFC North if they can find a way to upset Lamar Jackson and Co. at home. But this is the Browns we're talking about, so of course the football gods have seen fit to completely decimate Cleveland's backfield. Bellcow Quinshon Judkins left last week's loss to the New York Jets with an ankle injury after posting 44 yards on 14 carries. It's hard to overstate his importance to a Browns running back group that has essentially nothing in the way of proven production behind him. But while he's doing everything he can to suit up in Week 6 and seems to be trending in the right direction, his status remains very much up in the air just hours before kickoff. The fact that Judkins was able to at least get a practice in this week is a good sign that his injury isn't overly serious, as is the fact that the Browns opted not to call up another running back from the practice squad on Friday. home.headline: Lamar Jackson Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Ravens QB's Status for NFL Week 6 vs. Browns
home.blurb: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Jackson's status Friday, ruling him out for the matchup. ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that Jackson had a "realistic chance to return for Sunday's game," with Minter telling reporters that Jackson was considered day-to-day. Minter added that Jackson is "working his butt off" and "doing everything he can" to return to the field. Jackson was out for Week 5 as Tyler Huntley led the Ravens to an overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns as he continues to recover from an ankle injury. He initially left Week 4's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury and didn't play in the second half, a concerning development for a Ravens' offense very much reliant on the dynamic quarterback's unique skill set. While the Ravens didn't believe at the time that Jackson's injury was going to be a long-term issue, there was uncertainty over his short-term availability. "I really don't think it's going to be crazy long term, but we'll see what happens," head coach Jesse Minter told reporters at the time. There's no replacing a two-time MVP and three-time first-team All-Pro like Jackson, though the Ravens do have an experienced backup in Huntley. "There's one Lamar Jackson, the guy's a two-time MVP," Minter said after Week 4. "And so I think for anybody to have to say we're being compared to Lamar is unfair and not realistic. I think [Huntley] as a backup quarterback in this league and even as a starter at times has shown the ability to come in and really kind of run the offense, make plays with his legs, be able to make plays on third down." Injuries were also a concern for Jackson last season, as he missed four games due to a hamstring injury and a back contusion. Huntley started two of those games, leading the team to a 2-0 record. picks.headline: Why the Titans Will Beat the Colts in Week 6, Why They Won't, and a Prediction
picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Colts in Week 6, Why They Won't, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI For the fifth straight week in a row now, we can say that the Tennessee Titans fell short of expectations. What was initially painted as a bounce-back campaign for Robert Saleh and the franchise has turned into a recurring question from fans in Nashville: "How much longer will it take for this thing to change?" The answer? I wish I could give it to you. Instead, the Tennessee Titans stand alongside the Miami Dolphins as one of the only two teams without a win this season. On the road against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6, it no longer appears to be about things changing in the present. At this point, any sign of life on the way to a victory would do. In the split spirit of both optimism and reality, here's one reason the Titans will beat the Colts tomorrow, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction to split the difference. Will: Robert Saleh's defense bounces back Oct 11, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh walks onto the field during pre-game warmups against the Houston Texans at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Facing off with CJ Stroud and the Texans last Sunday, Robert Saleh's defense looked the worst they have all season. Saleh was in a direct battle with fellow defensive mind DeMeco Ryans, and beyond any doubt, he lost. Facing off with CJ Stroud and the Texans last Sunday, Robert Saleh's defense looked the worst they have all season. Saleh was in a direct battle with fellow defensive mind DeMeco Ryans, and beyond any doubt, he lost. Stroud threw for 261 yards and a score on 26 completions. The QB also found a touchdown on the ground as Houston ran away with a 26-3 victory. If Tennessee wins this week, it will be by slowing down a hot Colts offense with a massive recovery. Shut down Jonathan Taylor in the backfield, and who knows how far this team can get. Positively, Tennessee has done a solid job stopping the run this year in large part. The Texans rushed for just 79 yards last week in total. With star WR Alec Pierce on IR and reserve Ashton Dulin also set to miss time, QB Daniel Jones' options will be relatively limited. A Titans win would be about finding spurts of offensive momentum by way of defensive playmaking. Won't: Cam Ward continues to decline The lack of that offensive momentum, however, is the exact reason why Tennessee could come up short. Second-year QB Cam Ward has failed to generate any real momentum under center this season, and his shortcomings have the Titans punching up to begin with. Against Houston, Ward took four sacks and threw an interception for the third straight game. He's thrown less than 200 yards in four of the Titans' five games (five losses) this season. His full total is now out to three scores and three interceptions. That simply won't cut it for Tennessee's needed franchise QB. Promising weapons surrounding Ward, such as Wan'Dale Robinson and Carnell Tate in the WR room, haven't been able to elevate his underwhelming run. If the Titans fall short, you can safely bet it will be due to Ward once again falling short of the bar. Prediction: Titans lose, 27-17 Much like the Titans' early-season loss to the Texans last season (in which Tennessee went scoreless), I expect a relative surge of momentum from the offense. However, I don't expect the Titans to find a road win as they did vs. the Cardinals in 2025. Indy, while coming off a loss to the Steelers, has already collected two wins and consistently scored 20+ points. Their lone contest failing that margin came against Houston, in a 19-17 victory. Daniel Jones passes twice as much as Cam Ward (hardly hyperbole), and Taylor remains one of the NFL's premier backs. I predict Tennessee will surpass their three-point showing from Week 5, and things may even appear interesting early on. Still, there's nothing of present about this Titans team to suggest that a breakthrough is on the horizon. In an AFC South-bound duel tomorrow, I unfortunately anticipate the losing streak to continue. All we can hope for is a surprise from Saleh and a squad that, up to now, haven't done near enough to spark midseason hope. After an 0-5 start this season, the Titans are now 3-19 in the Cam Ward era and have not looked like a competent offense. Tennessee is a massive long shot to make the playoffs, but this is a potential spot for it to get a win against a Colts defense that was picked apart by the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 5. Indy is on the outside looking in of the playoff picture in the AFC, and the magic that it had before Jones was injured last season appears to be long gone. Oddsmakers have set the Colts as seven-point favorites at home in Week 6, making this one of the larger spreads of the week. Does Indy have enough firepower to win and cover against a division opponent? All season long, the SI Betting team is predicting the final score of every NFL game – a fun way to help bettors decide on their spread, moneyline and total bets. And, there’s a small chance that we’ll hit an exact score in the process! This AFC South matchup has major implications for the Colts and their playoff hopes, so let’s dive right into the odds and my score prediction for Sunday’s game. Titans vs. Colts Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Titans +7 (-115) Colts -7 (-105) 44.5 (Over -102/Under -118) This line has not moved much since opening , though it does appear that the total could close at 44 or 43.5 based on the latest odds. The Colts are heavily favored to win this game and send the Titans to 0-6 in 2026. Titans vs. Colts Score Prediction SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan has taken on the challenge of betting on every NFL game this season in his Road to 272 column . Earlier this week, he explained why he’s betting on Tennessee to win outright: You might be surprised to find out how many metrics these two teams rank similarly in, even some that the Titans outrank the Colts in, like net yards per play, which has the Titans at -0.7 and the Colts second-last in the NFL at -1.6. Another interesting metric for this game is that the Titans have the second-highest run frequency in neutral game states, meaning on early downs in the middle of the game when they still have a more than 20% win probability, Tennessee loves to run the football. That could be an area they exploit in this game, as the Colts rank dead last in the NFL in opponent rush EPA and 30th in opponent run success rate. Meanwhile, the Titans rank 16th and 11th in those two run defense categories, which will go a long way in slowing down Jonathan Taylor, which is the key to beating this Colts team. Even though Ward and the Titans have been downright awful on offense, ranking dead last in yards per play, 31st in EPA/Play and 26th in success rate during their 0-5 start, the Indy defense has been almost as bad. The Colts are allowing the third-most yards per play in the NFL on defense, ranking 27th in EPA/Play and 26th in success rate. That makes it really hard to lay this many points with the Colts, especially since they haven’t finished a ton of drives with touchdowns in 2026. I’m not as bold as MacMillan, but I do think there’s a case for the Titans to at least cover the spread in this game. The Titans are 4-5-1 against the spread on the road in the Cam Ward era, and I think they get back to .500 against the number in Week 6. The Indianapolis Colts return home to host the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, Oct. 18, with Indy as the near-touchdown favorite despite some concerning underlying metrics. My Titans vs. Colts prediction sees value in Tennessee ahead of this AFC South showdown, with the Titans' defense giving them a legitimate chance to make things uncomfortable at Lucas Oil Stadium. Here are my NFL picks ahead of this divisional clash, with kickoff set for 1 p.m. ET on FOX. TOP Pick Titans vs Colts prediction today: Titans +6.5 It's ugly, but I'd trade the Tennessee Titans +6.5, down to +5.5 , against the Indianapolis Colts . This is more of an anti-Indianapolis pick than pro-Tennessee. The Colts are 31st in net yards per play, 29th in early-down EPA per play differential, and 32nd in net quarterback pressure rate. I know the Titans suck, but should any team with that type of profile be a 6.5-point favorite? Also, after starting out last season hot, his first in Indianapolis, QB Daniel Jones is back to being terrible . Jones is 24th in adjusted EPA per play, according to RBSDM.com , and 26th in QBR. The bottom line: Jones and the Colts aren't good enough to be laying this many points . Titans vs Colts combo A Tennessee cover should correlate with an ugly, lower-scoring game, so I'm pairing Titans +6.5 with Under 44.5 and RB Tony Pollard 60+ rushing yards. Tennessee needs to shorten this game and keep QB Cam Ward out of obvious passing situations. That means establishing the run with Pollard against an Indianapolis defense ranked 27th in yards per rush allowed . That ground-heavy approach helps the Under. Neither offense has been trustworthy on late downs, and Tennessee and Indianapolis are tied for 24th in third-down conversion rate. A competitive game featuring long possessions, field goals, and limited explosive passing plays is exactly what I'm looking for. Tony Pollard Over 59.5 rushing yards Titans vs Colts player prop: Tony Pollard 60+ rushing yards Running back Tony Pollard 's rushing-yards prop is set against a Colts defense that ranks last in the NFL in rushing EPA per play allowed and run-stop win rate, according to ESPN. Pollard has cleared his rushing-yards prop in seven of his last 10 games , averaging 77.3 rushing yards per contest during that stretch. With Tennessee expected to keep Sunday's game competitive, Pollard should see more carries as the Titans look to establish the run against Indy's struggling defense. Want more NFL player props? Check out our NFL player prop projections ! Titans vs Colts touchdown scorer: Carnell Tate I'd trade Carnell Tate 's anytime touchdown probability up to 30%. Tate, the first receiver selected in the 2026 NFL Draft at No. 4 overall, is overdue for his first score. He has 37 targets this season, and Atlanta's Drake London is the only other pass-catcher with at least 37 targets who still doesn't have a receiving touchdown. The matchup also helps. All five Indianapolis starting defensive backs have failing PFF grades , while the Colts rank 22nd in defensive dropback EPA per play, according to RBSDM.com. If there's ever a spot for Tate to finally break through, this is it. John Lanfranca Sun, October 18, 2026 at 4:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tennessee Titans (0-5) and Indianapolis Colts (2-3) will clash in Week 6 of the NFL season this afternoon. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Indiana. The game will broadcast live on FOX. The Colts are 6.5-point favorites over the Titans on the spread, with the over/under set at 43.5 total points. Indianapolis is a -280 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Tennessee is priced as a +230 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Titans vs Colts predictions and NFL picks for Sunday, October 18. Titans vs Colts pick: Titans +7 (-120) My Colts vs. Titans best bet is Tennessee to cover the spread. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Download the Action Network app now for more NFL picks and analysis! Titans vs Colts Odds for NFL Week 6 Titans vs Colts spread: Titans +6.5 (-105), Colts -6.5 (-115) Titans vs Colts total: over/under 43.5 Titans vs Colts moneyline: Titans +230, Colts -280 Tennessee Titans vs Indianapolis Colts Preview The Titans may be near the bottom of any NFL power rankings you come across, but there is plenty of reason to believe they can compete with the Colts — and potentially pull the outright upset today. Indianapolis shouldn't be a touchdown favorite against any NFL team, even in a game it is projected to win on home turf. Let's start with what the Colts do well: run the football. Tennessee is sixth in the league defending the run on a per-carry basis despite playing from behind consistently. Even in a blowout loss to the Texans a week ago, the Titans limited the run effectively. It is evident they are playing the run more soundly this season — the Texans averaged just 2.9 yards per carry on 27 rushing attempts . In Week 4, Derrick Henry carried the ball 23 times against the Titans but averaged just 3.2 yards per rush. The Colts' Jonathan Taylor is an excellent back, but even he will struggle to gain consistent yardage if he is hit at or behind the line of scrimmage, something that has happened on 50% of his carries this season. The offensive line play for the Colts has been subpar through five games. Center Tanor Bortolini has played considerably worse this season than last, grading out 28th out of 34 qualifying players at the position, per Pro Football Focus. His matchup with Jeffery Simmons is one he simply cannot win on his own. Bortolini will need constant help with double teams in his attempt to negate the havoc Simmons can create. The issue for the Colts' front is that Simmons has John Franklin-Myers as his interior running mate. Both Franklin-Myers and Simmons rank inside the top 10 at the position this season in rush defense grade, per PFF. Running the ball is crucial for the Colts because their air attack lacks an explosive element without Alec Pierce in the lineup. In total, Indy ranks 30th in expected points added (EPA) as a passing offense. Daniel Jones has yet to crack seven yards per attempt in any game this season. Jones has a 4.6% turnover-worthy throw rate in comparison to a minuscule 2.0% big-time throw rate. Also, 19.9% of Jones' passes have been deemed off-target. That puts him in a tier with other quarterbacks who lead the league in inaccurate passes, with the only discernible difference being that the handful of other signal callers joining him in that tier have a considerably higher average depth of target . Cam Ward's performance to begin his second season with the Titans hasn't been very encouraging. However, this is by far the easiest matchup he has had this year. Ward's passer rating from a clean pocket sits at a respectable 96.1. It is pressure that gives him fits. The good news for the Tennessee offense here is that no team struggles to generate pressure more than Indianapolis. The Colts' pressure rate of 23% ranks last in the NFL. In fact, the gap between their pressure rate and the Cardinals ' pressure rate — the team that ranks 31st — is the same margin between the team ranking 14th ( Commanders ) and Arizona. Ward will have time to operate inside the pocket and the likelihood of him committing a game-changing turnover diminishes greatly in an environment in which he should be protected. In addition to lacking a pass rush, the Colts also rank last in the league in EPA/play when defending the run this season. Opposing rushers are averaging 2.4 yards before contact per rush against (31st). Titans vs Colts Pick, Betting Analysis You don't get many opportunities like this when diving into the ultra-tight market that is the NFL. We are able to back a team with a full touchdown worth of points in a divisional game where they are playing an opponent near the bottom of the league in passing offense, rushing defense, and pass rush production. There are a few books offering the Titans at +7 with added juice of just a few cents. away.headline: Colts' Week 6 injury report gives fans every reason to expect a Titans win
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts must feel pretty good about their health because they released Darius Slayton even though the team has struggled with wide receiver injuries this season. Not so much in Week 6, even though Ashton Dulin (hamstring) is going to be out and Alec Pierce still is . The positive is that Indy has a bye week, also known as having a matchup against the Tennessee Titans. As for Alec Pierce, no timeline exists for when he might return after reinjuring his heel. That might not happen until midseason, and the Colts will probably have far tougher games than the Titans before Pierce comes back. Besides Dulin, the only Indy player who will miss the game, according to head coach Shane Steichen , is linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs), but both Carlies and Dulin missed Week 5, and the reason the team lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers had nothing to do with the absences of Dulin and Carlies. The reason was that the defense was terrible again. Therein lies the difference between the Steelers and the Titans, as no matter how bad Indy's defense can be at times, Tennessee doesn't have the offensive talent that Pittsburgh has. Indianapolis Colts should be healthy enough to easily defeat the Tennessee Titans in Week 6 The Titans are 31st in the NFL in yards per play (4.5), last in points scored (58), 28th in quarterback rating (77.2), and 27th in rushing yards per game (82.6). Unless Indianapolis was without defensive lineman DeForest Buckner, cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward, and most other good starters, Indianapolis should be able to outscore Tennessee easily. And Buckner, Ward, and Gardner are healthy and will play in Week 6. The Titans haven't beaten Indianapolis since October 2022, a stretch of six straight wins for the Colts, and Indy has no excuse for not making that seven straight victories at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday. Injuries won't be a problem for the Colts, at least heading into the game. Tennessee won't have starting safety Kevin Winston Jr., but otherwise they are mostly healthy. They just don't have a lot of talent. They haven't defeated any AFC South team since January 2024, and if that changes against the Colts in Week 6, Indianapolis needs to make some immediate changes. Ultimately, Sunday should be a get-healthy game for the Indianapolis Colts as far as record and standing in the division. When all else is going on, at least Indianapolis can count on two wins every season against the dismal Tennessee Titans . Head coach Aaron Glenn's team has already exceeded expectations, staying competitive in every single one of its games this season while claiming a couple of victories against the Tennessee Titans and the Cleveland Browns. Meanwhile, the Patriots have rebounded from a slow start, rattling off two consecutive wins against the Buffalo Bills and the Las Vegas Raiders to round out a 3-2 record. Moving past another divisional opponent would keep New England in contention for the AFC East crown early in the season. As many expected coming into the campaign, the strength of this Jets team is its defense. Rookie defensive end David Bailey already has five sacks while four other players have two. New York is yet to force many turnovers, but the offense has been so good at limiting its own that it has not been much of a factor. The only giveaway that the Jets have on their stat sheet is a lost fumble from rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq, indicating a competent level of play from quarterback Geno Smith, who has managed every game adequately thus far. New England's defense will provide Smith with one of his biggest challenges of the season. Head coach Mike Vrabel's unit has forced six turnovers through five games, largely because of an excellent secondary led by cornerback Christian Gonzalez. It helps that defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr has created a scheme that consistently fools opposing passers, utilizing a variety of blitzes, rotations, and coverages to force offensive indecision on a snap-to-snap basis. With quarterback Drake Maye playing increasingly well, New England once again looks like a serious playoff contender in a crowded AFC. away.headline: New York Jets May Face A.J. Brown in New England Patriots Game - Report
away.blurb: Brown was listed as questionable on the Patriots injury report, and the team has not yet officially confirmed his return. If he does play, he opens up a major downfield threat for the Patriots. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye got off to a bad start this season, with just one touchdown pass in the first three games to go with six interceptions. But he rallied to form in back-to-back wins against the Buffalo Bills and the Las Vegas Raiders, racking up 643 passing yards to go with seven touchdowns against just one interception. Brown’s return would likely open up even more possibilities. The New York Jets’ chances of an upset win against the New England Patriots may get harder if an expected personnel move comes to fruition. A source told NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport that star receiver A.J. Brown is likely to be activated by the Patriots in time for Sunday’s game against the Jets. Brown missed the last four games with a high ankle sprain on his right leg. Brown, 29 years old, is a three-time Pro Bowl receiver. He was acquired from the Eagles in the offseason for a 2028 first-round draft pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder. Brown caught three passes for 26 yards in the Patriots opener on Sept. 9 against the Seattle Seahawks. He suffered a high ankle sprain in the third quarter, and the Patriots went on to lose 13-10 in a rematch of last season’s Super Bowl teams. In Brown’s absence, the Patriots made do with a receiving corps featuring Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III. “We’ve got a lot of guys that have made plays now, so it’s going to be tough on defenses,” Maye said earlier this week. “But I know we’ve got a tough challenge this week, so looking forward to it.” The Jets and Patriots will square off at 1 p.m. on Sunday at Gillette Stadium in Foxboro, Massachusetts. The Patriots are currently 7.5 point favorites.

home.headline: NFL insiders provide injury updates for Patriots' TreVeyon Henderson, Will Campbell
home.blurb: The New England Patriots added a pair of key players to their growing list of injury concerns during their blowout win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday as running back TreVeyon Henderson and left tackle Will Campbell each exited and did not return. The team has also been shorthanded at wide receiver. Offseason acquisition A.J. Brown suffered a high ankle sprain in the team's season opener and hasn't played since, though according to multiple reports he could be nearing a return. In addition, Mack Hollins was placed on injured reserve with a calf injury he suffered against the Bills. October 13, 2026 / 2:41 PM EDT / CBS Boston On Tuesday, NFL insiders provided updates on both Henderson and Campbell's injuries. Of the pair, the news was worse for Henderson. According to Adam Schefter of ESPN , the running back suffered a high ankle sprain in the second quarter of Sunday's game and is expected to miss multiple weeks. According to Schefter, Henderson will not require surgery and the team is hoping he will be back "relatively soon." The news was slightly better for Campbell, whose right knee got rolled up on, also in the second quarter. It was the same knee that Campbell hurt last year. Last season, he was placed on injured reserve. When he returned to action, Campbell wasn't the same player for the stretch run as New England made it all the way to the Super Bowl. Following Sunday's injury, Tom Pelissero reported that Campbell avoided a major knee injury. The NFL insider reported that Campbell is considered week-to-week. Rookie first-round draft pick Caleb Lomu would likely replace Campbell at left tackle should he be forced to miss time. Lomu came in following Campbell's injury and performed well against the Raiders. The Patriots have won back-to-back games despite a growing injury list. Star cornerback Christian Gonzalez missed both games, and fellow defensive back Carlton Davis joined him as inactive against the Raiders. Head coach Mike Vrabel was asked after Sunday's game how the team has embraced the next man up mentality. "Because that's what it has to be. You know what I mean? It's, we try not to panic," Vrabel said. "We just try to get the next guy ready. home.headline: New York Jets May Face A.J. Brown in New England Patriots Game - Report
home.blurb: Brown was listed as questionable on the Patriots injury report, and the team has not yet officially confirmed his return. If he does play, he opens up a major downfield threat for the Patriots. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye got off to a bad start this season, with just one touchdown pass in the first three games to go with six interceptions. But he rallied to form in back-to-back wins against the Buffalo Bills and the Las Vegas Raiders, racking up 643 passing yards to go with seven touchdowns against just one interception. Brown’s return would likely open up even more possibilities. The New York Jets’ chances of an upset win against the New England Patriots may get harder if an expected personnel move comes to fruition. A source told NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport that star receiver A.J. Brown is likely to be activated by the Patriots in time for Sunday’s game against the Jets. Brown missed the last four games with a high ankle sprain on his right leg. Brown, 29 years old, is a three-time Pro Bowl receiver. He was acquired from the Eagles in the offseason for a 2028 first-round draft pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder. Brown caught three passes for 26 yards in the Patriots opener on Sept. 9 against the Seattle Seahawks. He suffered a high ankle sprain in the third quarter, and the Patriots went on to lose 13-10 in a rematch of last season’s Super Bowl teams. In Brown’s absence, the Patriots made do with a receiving corps featuring Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III. “We’ve got a lot of guys that have made plays now, so it’s going to be tough on defenses,” Maye said earlier this week. “But I know we’ve got a tough challenge this week, so looking forward to it.” The Jets and Patriots will square off at 1 p.m. on Sunday at Gillette Stadium in Foxboro, Massachusetts. The Patriots are currently 7.5 point favorites.

The Saints have the league’s 20th-ranked offense (322.0 yards per game) and the 25th-ranked defense (361.0 yards per game) as they head into MetLife Stadium against a Giants team that has a chance to go 4-0 at home for the first time since 2008, when they got off to a 6-0 start at home. Despite the Saints’ struggles, they enter this game as a 1.5-point favorite per FanDuel , which is a head-scratcher considering they have averaged 21.3 points in their last three games, while the home team has averaged 25 points per game. But odds aside, the NFC East-leading Giants’ goal, according to head coach John Harbaugh, is simple: stack wins. “You always know what they are, but you know you’ve got to stack wins to make the December standings matter,” Harbaugh said when asked how much he pays attention to the standings at this point in the season. “So, we focus on the next game.” The Giants, according to Tankathon , have to make hay, so to speak. They face a remaining schedule with a combined winning percentage of .484, with their four toughest opponents being the 49ers, Jaguars, Lions, and Browns. All four of those challenging opponents land on the schedule after the Giants’ Week 8 bye. But to focus on what the Giants might do this week, let’s look at the best- and worst-case scenarios. If there was ever a good week for the Giants’ rushing game to snap out of its funk, this would be it. The league’s 30th-ranked run defense has struggled big time this season, allowing 4.9 yards per rushing attempt. It also ranks last in the league in defensive rush success (52.5%), meaning it struggles to stop opponents from gaining the minimum required yardage on a run (excluding kneeldowns and scrambles). The Giants’ rushing offense has not been the same since quarterback Jaxson Dart landed on IR with a season-ending knee injury. Although it ranks 17th in total rushing yards, it also averages a dismal 3.7 yards per attempt, 24th in the league. As if the rushing game’s struggles aren’t enough, it will be interesting to see if Harbaugh decides to reduce running back Cam Skattebo’s touches this week given his fumbling issue. As usual, the head coach was mum on the plans, but this could be a week when Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy Jr. get bigger roles in the rushing attack to see if they can jumpstart it. On the defensive side, the Giants’ pass rush has finally awakened after a slow start, recording seven sacks over the last two weeks. This week, they face a Saints offensive line that has surrendered three sacks to quarterback Tyler Shough over that same period. Combine that with the opportunistic Giants secondary, which has forced eight turnovers this season , against a Saints offense that has committed 13 giveaways, and the Giants’ quest to remain undefeated at home could get a lot easier. Why the Giants Won’t Beat the Saints Oct 5, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara (41) scores a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the first half at Caesars Superdome. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Giants’ run defense, in Harbaugh’s words, has been “feast or famine” this season. The Giants’ run defense, in Harbaugh’s words, has been “feast or famine” this season. Last week in the tie against Washington, it was clearly the latter, having surrendered a season-high 202 yards on the ground. There are many reasons for the Giants’ struggles in run defense, but one glaring issue has been facing pre-snap motion. Motion changes the look for the defense and has sometimes left players out of position or forced them into bad angles as they try to stop the play from gaining a lot of yards. Under head coach Kellen Moore, the Saints have deployed pre-snap motion on 64% of their offensive snaps this season, the ninth-highest rate in the league, and have a 46% success rate overall when using motion. While they use pre-snap motion more in the passing game, they have used it at a 35% rate in the rushing game. If the Giants, who have allowed opponents 5.2 yards per rush attempt on first down, can’t tighten that up, the Saints will have options on subsequent downs, giving New Orleans an advantage. The other thing that could spoil the Giants’ quest to win their fourth straight game at home is their own aggressiveness on defense. If the Giants, who over the last two weeks have blitzed on 57.8% of opposing quarterbacks’ drop backs, come at the Saints with a similar rate of pressure, they’d better hope that Saints signal-caller Tyler Shough, who per PFF data, has a 102.7 passer rating when throwing the ball in 2.5 seconds or less, doesn’t connect with receivers Chris Olave and Rashid Shaheed for the big pass plays downfield. If I live to be 100 (fingers crossed), I will never understand how the oddsmakers come up with their weekly point spreads. What I do understand is that Harbaugh has this team dialed in, and this matchup against the Saints is overall favorable for the Giants if they play a relatively clean game and keep the ball-security issues out of the mix. The Giants have a lot more going for them at this point in the season than the Saints, including far too many advantages that, if they hit on all cylinders, will get the job done. Following a frustrating 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings , the Saints (1-4) have dropped three consecutive games, raising questions about the team's direction under second-year head coach Kellen Moore. The struggles have even drawn the attention of team owner Gayle Benson , who recently expressed frustration with the organization's performance and made it clear that continued losing would not be tolerated without consequences. With expectations rising and patience wearing thin, New Orleans faces another difficult challenge against a surprising Giants team that has emerged as an early contender in the NFC East. Here are our predictions for Sunday's game. Grant Chachere, Staff Writer: L 24-17 This is the Saints' first road game since Week 2, and it’s a strategic one at that, as the Saints will immediately fly out of New York for their game against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris next week. However, this is a critical game for coach Kellen Moore , and maybe even longtime general manager Mickey Loomis . I don’t think Tyler Shough will have many games like he did last week in the loss to the Vikings, but he will have another matchup against a top-10 defense as the Giants are ninth in total defense. The strength of the defense is its ability to defend the pass, allowing only 199.7 yards per contest, which is good for seventh in the NFL, and have forced six interceptions, which is good for fourth. While I think Shough will do much better, the Giants have the players needed to at least limit Shough, and New Orleans’ rushing attack is one of the NFL’s worst and will be ineffective. While the Giants have struggled to stop the run, they will have no trouble stopping the Saints. At the half, join us for Halftime Studs & Duds . Then, a fter the game, join us for our Biggest Winners & Biggest Losers , our View of the Game , and the Most Important Quotes from Kellen Moore & Players . Defensively, I think the Saints will do enough to keep the game close but not enough to win. The Giants aren’t the greatest offense in the world, but Cam Skattebo is a decent running back, while the receiving threats of Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are going to give the Saints’ defense a heap of trouble. I predict a one-score game in the Meadowlands with the Giants pulling it out. Prediction: Giants 24, Saints 17 Doug Joubert, Publisher: W 21-17 Which Saints club will show in the Meadowlands today? Will it be the one from the first three weeks of the season, or the one from the last three? We know this: those leading this organization have been put on notice by the woman that holds the checkbook. For the first time as owner of the Saints, Gayle Benson is faced with a situation that will require resolve and a possible move that will force her to make decisions that will be uncomfortable. She has put her trust and belief in those in charge. After seeing where her club has gone in the last few weeks, and the fan reaction to that direction, Mrs. Benson is having to rethink that trust. Meanwhile, a two-week road trip followed by the Saints open/bye week may be just what the doctor ordered for Moore and his troops: a chance to regroup and rethink where things are. Being a "glass-half-full" kinda guy, I'm getting this feeling this may be the first step to Moore, his coaches, and his players turning things around. However, don't bet the house on who I choose to win today. I've only been right once in five prognostications this year. Stuckey Sun, October 18, 2026 at 3:54 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New Orleans Saints (1-4) and New York Giants (3-1-1) will square off in Week 6 of the NFL season this afternoon. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The game will broadcast live on FOX. The Saints are 1.5-point favorites over the Giants on the spread, with the over/under set at 45.5 total points. New Orleans is a -115 moneyline favorite to win outright, while New York is listed as a -105 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Saints vs Giants predictions and NFL picks for Sunday, October 18. Saints vs Giants pick: Saints -1.5 (+100) My Giants vs. Saints best bet is New Orleans to cover the spread (-1.5), with the best price currently available at FanDuel . Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Download the Action Network app now for more NFL picks and analysis! Saints vs Giants Odds for NFL Week 6 Saints vs Giants spread: Saints -1.5, Giants +1.5 Saints vs Giants total: over/under 45.5 Saints vs Giants moneyline: Saints -115, Giants -105 New Orleans Saints vs New York Giants Preview The Saints originally opened as underdogs for this game, but almost immediately swung to 1.5-point road favorites — and I think they are sitting at the absolute bottom of their market value. Am I thrilled to back New Orleans on the road here? Not exactly. But I am itching to fade the Giants . Sure, the Saints' run defense is abysmal, but they are facing a Giants team entirely incapable of exploiting it. New Orleans has played a grueling schedule the last two weeks, facing the Falcons (who ran wild with Bijan Robinson) and the Vikings (who have one of the best defenses in the NFL). Offensively, Tyler Shough has been very good when kept clean in the pocket. With the Giants missing Brian Burns , Shough should have all day to operate and consistently move the ball through the air in this game. The Giants are a couple games above .500, but they are arguably the most fraudulent team in the NFL. They could easily be 1-4 right now after lucking out with a tie against the Commanders last week. New York's back-to-back home wins came against the Titans and Cardinals — two incompetent teams that turned the ball over at the goal line with a chance to win. Offensively, the Giants have completely stalled since losing Jaxson Dart. They rank 29th in both rush success rate and rush EPA, meaning their ground game has almost totally vanished. Jameis Winston has thrown for 694 yards with a 6:3 TD:INT ratio in the three games he's started. He's done a good job of feeding Malik Nabers as the Giants' WR1 has surpassed 100 receiving yards in each of the last two weeks. Of course, the thing with Winston is that he's prone to making critical mistakes when throwing into zone coverage. Saints vs Giants Pick, Betting Analysis There is a massive strength-of-schedule disparity here, with the Giants feasting on the easiest schedule in the league so far while the Saints have been heavily battle tested against some of the NFL's best.
