away.blurb: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin) and linebacker Abdul Carter (calf) are both expected to play despite being listed as questionable. Thomas has managed his groin issue since Week 2 without missing a snap, while Carter’s expected return provides a boost to a defense already without Brian Burns for the season. Right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) was not addressed by Rapoport. away.headline: Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out?
away.blurb: The Giants ruled out safety Tyler Nubin (neck), tight end Theo Johnson (neck), and cornerback Colton Hood (concussion). WR Chris Olave (illness) didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday, but he was able to work on a limited basis during Friday's practice. He should play so long as that illness is behind him. DL Nathan Shepherd (illness) also missed two days of practice with an illness that's been going around the locker room. He was limited on Friday as well. CB Lorenzo Styles Jr. (knee) was limited on both Thursday and Friday, so don't be surprised if he's a game-time decision. RB Alvin Kamara (back) practiced on limited reps throughout the week. The Saints didn't bring up either of the two running b acks on their practice squad so it does llook like he'll play. Starting offensive linemen Andrew Thomas (groin) and Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) are both questionable for the Giants, as is edge rusher Abdul Carter (calf). There's a crowd of Giants players available to play after being listed on the injury report this week: cornerback Greg Newsome II (groin), outside linebacker Malik Harrison (groin), defensive back Elijah Campbell (thumb), running back Najee Harris (ribs), tight end Isaiah Likely (foot), wide receivers Darnell Mooney (neck) and Charlie Jones (Achilles), as well as safety Jason Pinnock (concussion). As was the case last week, the following Saints players are on injured reserve with season-ending injuries: defensive tackle Bryan Bresee, running back Ty Chandler, cornerback David Long Jr., tight end Moliki Matavao, offensive lineman Dillon Radunz, and cornerback Rejzohn Wright. However, a couple of others have been designated to return after sitting out at least four games: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and veteran running back Travis Etienne Jr. are both expected to return after the bye week in November but it sounds like we won't see left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. until December at the soonest. Offensive lineman Nick Saldiveri is on the season-ending PUP list (physically unable to perform), while wide receiver Mason Tipton is eligible to return after missing four games. Tipton has not returned to practice yet. LS Zach Wood (calf) returned from injured reserve and is expected to play. The Saints don't have another long snapper on the roster. DL Davon Godchaux (not injury related/rest) OL Jeremiah Wright (concussion)

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 6 schedule, including five locks against the spread Getty Images I don't know what it is about the Week 6 slate, but I think we're going to have some underdogs bark rather loudly. I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here. Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5 New York Jets at New England Patriots I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. Meanwhile, they've also taken care of business against inferior opponents under Mike Vrabel as the Patriots are 11-0 with him at the helm when facing teams entering with a losing record. Further looking at the trends for this one, the Patriots are 12-0 straight-up and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 games as a favorite and have a +17.9 PPG differential over that stretch. As for the Jets , they've yet to win or cover (0-6) a divisional game under head coach Aaron Glenn. And few teams are more disappointing thus far than the Philadelphia Eagles . Might Nick Sirianni get a pink slip if his club loses at home Sunday against a rested and surging Carolina Panthers team? High 58F. Winds NW at 5 to 10 mph. With the Eagles -1.5 at DraftKings , 94% of ATS handle is on them but 55% of bets are on the Panthers. There's heavy action on the Over with a low total of 40.5. The latest odds I saw post-Week 5 on the first NFL head coach fired had Washington's Dan Quinn as the +200 favorite and Sirianni next at +400. And that's absolutely no surprise to me after both NFC East head coaches made utterly stupid decisions that cost their teams victories this past Sunday. I'm sure you know by know what happened in Commanders-Giants and Eagles-Jaguars. Quinn and/or Jayden Daniels didn't even get a field-goal try off at end of overtime, with a win in Washington's hands. Maybe that clock mistake was on Daniels, but there's no doubt it's on Sirianni for having Jake Elliott kick off into the Jacksonville landing zone on Sunday in London. That allowed a long return and a walk-off 57-yard field goal to win. All the Eagles had to do was kick the ball out of the end zone and the Jags are at their 35 hoping for a Hail Mary with no timeouts. Kudos to Sirianni for taking the blame, but he wouldn't take any for managing the prior scoring drive in a way that left the Jaguars with more time than they should have had. Two passes stopped the clock, and Elliott kicked the go-ahead field goal with 12 seconds left. Why not run it down to only a couple and make that the final play? "I'm honoring a play call, honoring the things that are coming in the game," QB Jalen Hurts said afterward. "We're not asking him to make play calls in that scenario," Sirianni responded to Monday. Starting to feel a disconnect there? The Eagles' next game is on a bit of extra rest, as it is Monday night in Week 7 vs. Dallas, so you might see a change if this goes badly Sunday, even though Sirianni is 67-33 as the Eagles head coach. That's tied for the fifth-best head coaching record through 100 games in the league since 1970. The team's bye isn't until Week 10, and you can already hear the Mike Tomlin rumors. This marks Sirianni's third three-game losing streak in Philadelphia, and he has never lost four in a row. It's not just his clock management, but his offense has been lousy during this skid in averaging 14.7 points and 217 yards per game while converting just 22.2% of third downs. The PPG is the fewest for Philly through five games since 2012, and the YPG the fewest through five since 1999. A juggled offensive line hasn't helped. With Lane Johnson having retired, Cam Jurgens traded and Landon Dickerson on injured reserve, the team has replaced three starters already. And it's not clear yet if the offense will have tailback and former NFL Offensive Player of the Year Saquon Barkley and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith back from injury yet, after both missed Week 5. The Eagles are averaging a scant 3.5 yards per play with both off the field this season, compared to 5.3 in all other situations. It's possible the Eagles are down to their No. 4 tailback because No. 2 Tank Bigsby is on IR and No. 3 Will Shipley was hurt against the Jags. This will mark the first time the Eagles will take the field sitting below .500 since 2021, when they were 6-7. The 76 straight games played without a losing record was the longest streak in team history. The overall NFL record is 145 by the Patriots from 2003-12. Carolina comes off its bye with its 2-2 mark the team's best four-game start since 2021. It's also good enough for the lead in the ultra-weak NFC South – the Panthers are +130 favorites. We get a former all-Alabama quarterback matchup here in Bryce Young vs. Hurts with Young off to his best start and perhaps answering all those lingering questions that have dogged the former No. 1 overall pick. Thanks to Young and sensational second-year wideout Tetairoa McMillan , the Panthers rank top five in the league in scoring offense (30.3 PPG), total offense (405.8 YPG) and passing offense (301.3 YPG). The scoring average is the best in franchise history through four games, and it's their first time averaging at least 30.0 PPG in any four-game span since 2019. Young would make history if he keeps his NFL-best 317.0-yard passing average up, as no QB ever has averaged even 275 yards passing in a season after three straight years under 200.0 passing yards per. Young also led the NFL entering his bye week with 11 completions on deep throws (20+ air yards). He is 0-1 against Hurts in the NFL as the Eagles beat the visiting Panthers 22-16 in the most recent meeting in December 2024. They're coming off a brilliant upset win over the Detroit Lions, too. The Philadelphia Eagles made the long trek back from London after a mindboggling, crushing defeat where victory was essentially secured. The Panthers have the advantage this week, it seems. Despite that, they're not favored on the road, and some experts aren't willing to pick the Panthers to take the Eagles down. Expert picks for Eagles vs. Panthers in NFL Week 6 action Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni reacts during the first half | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect CBS Sports' Pete Prisco has picked against the Panthers all season, his seeming disdain for the franchise refusing to go away. He isn't changing his ways this week, either, picking the Eagles to win by three despite giving ample reason the Panthers should win. CBS Sports' Pete Prisco has picked against the Panthers all season, his seeming disdain for the franchise refusing to go away. He isn't changing his ways this week, either, picking the Eagles to win by three despite giving ample reason the Panthers should win. "The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. Somehow, though, they will get off the deck to win this behind their defense," he wrote. His CBS colleague, Jordan Dajani, disagreed, picking the Panthers to win 23-21. "The Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS," Dajani pointed out. Here's how SI's staff is picking the game: Albert Breer: Panthers Eva Geitheim: Panthers Mitch Goldich: Eagles Mike Kadlick: Panthers Gilberto Manzano: Panthers Conor Orr: Eagles John Pluym: Eagles Matt Verderame: Eagles Bleacher Report's Wes O'Donnell is taking the Panthers to cover the spread and win outright. "I'm done trying to figure out the Eagles. The Eagles clearly cannot figure out the Eagles. And while the Panthers' defense is a great opportunity for any offense to get right, Carolina had a bye week and then some to prepare for Philly. This Panthers team has defied the odds and shown up in tough situations since last season," he wrote. Carolina Panthers head coach Dave Canales reacts after the game at Bank of America Stadium | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect His colleagues Gary Davenport, Kristopher Knox, Moe Moton, and Brent Sobleski agree, while Ian Hanford and Brad Gagnon disagree, picking the Eagles. His colleagues Gary Davenport, Kristopher Knox, Moe Moton, and Brent Sobleski agree, while Ian Hanford and Brad Gagnon disagree, picking the Eagles. At ESPN , only Pam Maldonado and Dan Graziano picked the Eagles to beat the Panthers. The Athletic's Vic Tafur was obscenely blunt: "The Eagles are coming off two heartbreaking losses, they struggle against play-action passes (a Panthers staple), and it wouldn’t shock me if this is Sirianni’s last game as head coach." What does this mean? Despite the overwhelming advantages the Panthers have in this game, there's still a perception that the Eagles are the Eagles and the Panthers are the woeful Panthers. That makes Week 6's contest a perfect opportunity to reshape the narrative, although it's a little unfair that a primetime victory over the Detroit Lions didn't do that for the Panthers. The Eagles' offense, meanwhile, is without Jalen Hurts. Saquon Barkley probably won't play. Will Shipley is out. Devonta Smith might miss Week 6, too. The Eagles just lost Lane Johnson (retirement) and Cam Jurgens (trade) on the offensive line. Where are they supposed to get any sort of production from? Everything says the Panthers should win this game, so naturally, they could find a way to lose it. But I think we've seen this year that these aren't the same old Panthers, and this is the sort of statement win they've been building to and getting more of over the last two seasons. Preston Palm: Panthers 27, Eagles 19 This feels like a trap game spot for the Panthers. Even with no Jalen Hurts, no Saquon Barkley, and a suspect offensive line, the Eagles are going to play Carolina close. away.headline: Carolina Panthers Injury Update: 2 Key Players Gearing up for Their Return
away.blurb: Carolina Panthers Injury Update: 2 Key Players Gearing up for Their Return - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Carolina Panthers Injury Update: 2 Key Players Gearing up for Their Return Fans of the Carolina Panthers have finally got some good news regarding injuries. For the past four weeks, whenever the injury banner pops up in their feed, Carolina Panthers fans have covered and resigned, expecting to see their favorite player out for an extended period of time. However, this week, Dave Canales spoke to the media with updates on Taylor Moton and Tershawn Wharton . Wharton had neck surgery back in May, also putting him on an unknown timetable for his return. He was immediately placed on the PUP list, and the Panthers have tried to fill his role as the interior speed rusher. While there has been some success with Pat Jones, who has also missed time, there has been limited production elsewhere. Rookie Lee Hunter has so far been the most effective defensive tackle next to Derrick Brown, but on obvious passing downs, his slow pass rush has been a hindrance at times. In the same press conference where coach Canales revealed that Moton and wharton's windows were open, he also revealed the fate of Trevor Etienne, who began the season on IR. Etienne injured his knee during the final roster cutdowns, allowing Carolina to keep an open roster slot while placing him on IR. He is now ready to make his return. While his production was limited in his rookie season, sitting behind Rico Dowdle and Chuba Hubbard, Etienne played well with special teams and passing situations for Carolina down the stretch in 2025. In a year where the Panthers again lost Johanthan Brooks to am extend groin injury, getting Etienne back to give Carolina running back room of three backs allows for Hubbard and Dillon to get much need resort during games, as well as a buffer in anymore unexpected injuries happen. Etienne will most likely return to his role in special teams, giving Carolina another player with kick and punt return experience to work with. The Carolina Panthers have been an injury riddle in the 2026 season. An early bye week came bearing fruit for the Panthers' injury news. Taylor Moton and Tershawn Wharton's return spells good things on the horizon for Carolina. Moton will allow Freeling to return to the development pool, allowing him to review his film, watch a Panthers staple on the right side, and learn from him. It will also give Freeling a chance to get healthier himself, after suffering a concussion and a knee injury in the last two weeks. Wharton's return means that Carolina might get a boost in pass rush. Wharton has always had the speed and strength to work from the inside, and adding him to a room with Jaelan Phillips and Princely Umanmielen means Carolina will have a perfect blend of speed and power. home.headline: Eagles will bring back Jalen Hurts this season under one condition amid blood clot issue: report
home.blurb: Hurts being placed on the IR means he has to miss a minimum of four games, but he is considering out "indefinitely" as the Eagles want to make sure his blood clot dissipates. "If he has a deep vein clot, he's out for multiple weeks, at least." Jalen Hurts is in a very serious injury situation with the Philadelphia Eagles , who placed him on the injured reserve as the quarterback deals with a blood clot. In fact, Jay Glazer said on "FOX NFL Sunday" that the Eagles would only bring back their franchise quarterback if the clot "completely melted. "At first, the blood clot was superficial; it wasn’t moving around," Glazer said on the pregame show. He noted that was why Hurts played against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London this past week. "But once it changed and that blood clot started moving, you do not mess around with a moving blood clot. That could be a life-or-death situation. "The only way really for Jalen Hurts to come back — if he can come back this season — is that blood clot needs to be completely melted. They have to have several different scans to make sure it’s completely gone. Because if it’s not, and if it floats up to the wrong areas, it’d be very, very dangerous." David Chao, who served as the Los Angeles Chargers’ team doctor for 17 years while they were in San Diego, told OutKick recently the same thing regarding the movement of the blood clot. "Do they mean movement as in it's propagating and it's now a bigger superficial blood clot? Or is it movement meaning it's deeper and it's a deep vein clot?" Chao questioned. With Hurts on the IR, the Eagles had Tanner McKee, his backup, make his first start of the season against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. The Eagles fell, 25-14, to their NFC foe with McKee throwing for 215 yards with a touchdown to DeVonta Smith. The Eagles will be without Hurts for at least next week’s "Monday Night Football" matchup against the Dallas Cowboys, "Sunday Night Football" against the Washington Commanders and a matchup with the New York Giants – all three NFC East divisional games. Injuries have been present throughout this 2026 campaign for Philadelphia outside of Hurts, with running back Saquon Barkley missing another game this Sunday as he deals with a hamstring injury. Running backs Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley also are dealing with ailments, while offensive lineman Lane Johnson surprised everyone with his retirement mid-season. The Bucs beat the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 last week, but now, they'll face a tougher defense and a legendary quarterback in Aaron Rodgers. As always, our staff has made its picks for Sunday's big cross-conference matchup in Tampa Bay. Here's how we see the Bucs' game against the Steelers shaping out: Caleb Skinner, Writer: Steelers 24, Bucs 20 The Bucs are coming off their first win of the season, and they have an excellent chance to continue that momentum against the Steelers. I expect the Bucs to continue being efficient on offense, so it will be up to the defense to stop Warren and not allow the playmakers for the Steelers to make big plays. I think the Bucs do, but aren’t able to come away with a clutch play that would give them the win. Overall Record: 3-2 James Hill, Writer: Steelers 21, Bucs 17 I believe this will be a low-scoring affair, as both defenses have the chance to be good. However, I give the nod to Aaron Rodgers over Jalon Daniels, who will get a start once more with Mayfield on the mend. Overall record: 2-3 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Bucs 21, Steelers 14 So far, the 2026 NFL season has been very deflating for a Buccaneers team that had plenty of optimism heading into it. But because they play in the NFC South, the Buccaneers aren’t dead yet. However, if they have any hope of turning their season around and eventually making a push for the playoffs, they need to build some momentum off their first victory of the year in Dallas last week. Defensively, the Bucs match up pretty well with the Steelers. Tampa Bay's corners have played out of their minds this season, and this will be their easiest matchup yet. That should allow Bowles to really sell out to stop the run led by Jaylen Warren, who has developed into the Steelers’ most dynamic offensive weapon. Jalon Daniels and Zac Robinson need to take care of the football and control the clock like they did against Dallas. If they can, the Bucs will win. Logan Robinson, Founder: Steelers 31, Bucs 24 This front seven for the Steelers is going to be a lot different than what Jalon Daniels has faced this season. Zac Robinson will want to get the run game going again with Bucky Irving, but it won’t be easy with Cam Heyward and others in the middle for Pittsburgh. I think this is a great game to take advantage of an immobile Aaron Rodgers and find multiple sacks throughout. If you can’t find sacks in this game, you’ve got issues going into the rest of the season. I think the Bucs keep this one close against a dinged-up Steelers team but don’t pull it off in the fourth quarter. River Wells, Editor: Steelers 24, Bucs 17 The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got a huge win against the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 last Thursday, and now, they'll try to pick up another with quarterback Jalon Daniels under center. The good news? This offense isn't nearly as good as Dallas' offense. The bad news? The defense is much better. The Bucs put up 24 against a paltry Dallas defense, so they should put up less against a more competent unit. T.J. Watt, with 4.5 sacks in five games, will be the best edge rusher the Bucs have faced so far this year, and he'll probably make Daniels' life hell for four quarters. On the offensive side for the Steelers, Aaron Rodgers' quick-fire short game matches up perfectly against Bowles' defense. Jaylen Warren is arguably the most dynamic player the Bucs have faced this year since Ja'Marr Chase, and he'll give Tampa Bay's defense fits, too. The Bucs could keep this close, but I think Pittsburgh takes it. Consensus: Steelers 4, Bucs 1 The Bucs got it done against Dallas, but most of our panel doesn't think they can get it done against the Steelers back at home. Will Daniels and the Bucs make it two in a row for the first time since the beginning of the 2025 season? Or will the Steelers knock the Bucs down to 1-5 on the year? At 1-4, the Bucs are only 1.5 games behind the Carolina Panthers in the weak NFC South division. However, Tampa must win a few more games before it can even start thinking about making the playoffs. Luckily, the Bucs have winnable games on the schedule over the next few weeks, including a pair against division rivals. However, Tampa has the Pittsburgh Steelers on the docket next, already the Bucs' third game against an AFC North foe. The Steelers are 3-2 and have been inconsistent this season, although their offense has turned a corner after a very slow start. The Bucs are 2.5-point underdogs at home, but managed to pull off the upset against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 5 as 9.5-point underdogs. Beating the Steelers will qualify as an upset, but it is a very winnable game for the Bucs. Aside from a non-existent pass rush, the Bucs' defense has been very good this season. Now it must contend with a red-hot Aaron Rodgers, who has thrown for three TDs in each of Pittsburgh's last three games. Steelers' RB Jaylen Warren has also been outstanding in the last three games, rushing for 127, 93, and 101 yards. He also caught an 80-yard TD last week, and his 230 receiving yards lead the team. Tampa's run defense is second in the NFL so far, and stopping Warren is one of my five keys to a Bucs' victory , as is finally getting the pass rush to show a pulse. On offense, the Bucs have a budding star in RB Bucky Irving, who is coming off a career-best 165 rushing yards and had both a rushing and a receiving TD against Dallas. For Tampa to win, Irving must continue to be the centerpiece of the offense. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will be making his third straight start while starting QB Baker Mayfield recovers from a dislocated thumb. Daniels has played with the poise of a seasoned veteran and earned the first victory of his career against the Cowboys. For Tampa to win, Daniels must once again play a clean, turnover-free game. The offensive line must keep Pittsburgh's pass rush, especially T.J. Watt, away from Daniels. This game is set to be a matchup of strengths against strengths. Warren is sixth in the NFL in rushing yards and will be going up against Tampa's strong run defense. Rodgers has been great over the last three weeks, but will have to make plays against a secondary that has shut down the star WR duos of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins and CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. The Steelers will be without WRs Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson in this game. If Irving can get going early, it will make life much easier for Daniels, whose ability to also make plays with his legs can be a huge factor, especially on third down. This game seems like it could go either way, with a turnover or missed kick looming large at game's end. away.headline: Steelers injury report: Pittsburgh enters road trip with abundance of injuries
away.blurb: Out of the bye, road trips to face the division rival Bengals and in-state rival Eagles await. Neither is a long trip in terms of mileage, but the Steelers have not won in Philadelphia since 1965, and it follows an AFC North dogfight. The receivers room is the most pressing problem. Pittman will be out for at least the next three games after being placed on injured reserve. The veteran was a key offseason acquisition but has only played in three games in which he's caught seven passes for 89 yards. The extent of the injuries to Wilson and Skowronek, sustained against Indianapolis, are not yet known, but McCarthy said Monday that both will be out for at least the Tampa Bay game. The secondary is a bit better off. Ramsey spent the week leading up to the Colts game on the injury report but handled a normal workload. Only Dean was absent, and the Steelers have not yet taken the step of adding the free agent cornerback signing to injured reserve. Dean was a limited practice participant Wednesday while Ramsey was out with a wrist injury listed. McCarthy hinted strongly that Dowdle is expected back this week from the toe injury he sustained in Week 2 against New England. He was also limited Wednesday. That should help the offense manage the reps of Jaylen Warren, who's handled a heavy workload in Dowdle's absence. home.headline: Buccaneers vs. Steelers: Final injury report for Week 6
home.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have released their final injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and several key players will be unavailable as Tampa Bay looks to build on last week's victory over Dallas. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb) has officially been ruled out after missing all three practices this week. Rookie Jalon Daniels will make his third consecutive start after leading the Buccaneers to their first victory of the season last Thursday against the Cowboys. The Buccaneers will also be without safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib), who did not participate in practice throughout the week. Wide receiver David Sills V (hamstring) was also ruled out despite being listed as a full participant in all three practices. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad) is listed as doubtful, while linebackers SirVocea Dennis (ankle/foot) and Josiah Trotter (knee), cornerback Ayden Garnes (ankle), and running back Sean Tucker (quad) are questionable. Dennis and Garnes were full participants Friday, providing some encouraging news heading into the weekend. Pittsburgh is also dealing with several injuries, particularly at wide receiver. Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have been ruled out, along with safety DeShon Elliott (knee). Wide receiver DK Metcalf was added to Friday's report with an illness and is questionable. Since then, Arizona has lost four straight games, allowing over 30 points in all of them. Plus, the team traded away former top-five pick Marvin Harrison Jr. in a deal with the Houston Texans. away.headline: Rams CB Trent McDuffie not playing today vs Cardinals after sudden groin injury as Cam Lampkin gets big break
away.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams' fears came true after cornerback Trent McDuffie, who was a game-time decision ahead of the Cardinals after suffering a groin injury in practice on Friday, was ruled out. Along with McDuffie, the Los Angeles Rams will also miss their emergency QB, Ty Simpson, as Matthew Stafford will continue on throwing duties. Wide receiver Tutu Atwell, defensive end Larrell Murchison and offensive lineman Bill Murray also remain out. The Los Angeles Rams have not provided details of the groin issue that Trent McDuffie suffered ahead of Friday's practice. Yahoo Sports reports that it is likely a full groin pull that the CB picked up later this week. It is unclear if he picked up the injury during practice. The Los Angeles Rams have also not provided a potential timeline for the 26-year-old cornerback's return. Keagen Trost, 25, was drafted by the Los Angeles Rams out of Missouri. Trost played 13 games for the Missouri Tigers in the SEC. In the 2024, he played 12 games for Wake Forest in the ACC. McDuffie is not playing in the Week 6 NFL game against the Arizona Cardinals, making it his first miss of the season. The Rams promoted Cam Lampkin, a defensive back from their practice squad to the active roster. It is likely that Cam Lampkin will have to handle the uphill task of keeping Eagles wide receiver Michael Wilson at bay. A surprise entry on the roster was Rookie offensive tackle Keagan Trost, who is on the active roster for the first time ever. He was picked up by the Los Angeles Rams in the third round of the 2026 NFL draft as the 93rd overall pick. What Happened To Trent McDuffie? Trent McDuffie has played all five of Rams regular season games so far. He has recorded 16 tackles (13 solo), one interception and defended seven passes. The Rams, with a 2-3 season so far, are still better off compared to their opponents, the Arizona Cardinals, who are 4th in the NFC West with a 1-4 season so far. The absence of Trent McDuffie is expected to open up a chance for the Cardinals to change the state of their season.

away.headline: Arizona Cardinals injury report: Jeremiyah Love sits Wednesday
away.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals opened their practice week Wednesday for Sunday’s road game against the Los Angeles Rams and released their first injury report of Week 5. Running back Jeremiyah Love did not practice. It appeared that LaFleur claimed Williams would be unavailable for Sunday’s game when he said, “He’s not going to clear the concussion protocol.” The report is an estimate because the Rams did not practice after playing the Buffalo Bills Monday night. Recovered from the right high-ankle sprain suffered in the Aug. 13 preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders , his left ankle has been an issue for several weeks. He has felt good heading into games, but then aggravation occurs on the field. Head coach Mike LaFleur said, “Want to get this ankle right and do it the right way. He’s a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. Imagine being a running back in the NFL, trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you’re capable of. We all are in agreeance, as much as he wants to battle through, we’re all in agreeance right now that (he needs to) give a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on what that’ll entail for Sunday.” Asked about concern about it continuing to be a problem going forward, LaFleur said, “It’s an ankle, so you don’t know. I’m not a doctor and each body is a little bit different. The way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable. He doesn’t even feel it, but this one is the one that happened when the regular season started and it’s just lingering.” The full details their Wednesday injury repory are below. home.headline: Rams have a legitimate gripe with NFL officials, but their 2-4 record is the bigger problem
home.blurb: Rams kicker Blake Grupe knocks himself out of his debut with a disastrous tackle attempt Yes, a questionable personal foul helped Arizona get into position for the winning field goal in its 18-16 victory. Rams fans have every right to be frustrated, especially given what happened against Denver earlier this season. Rams kicker Blake Grupe had injured his knee tackling Devin Duvernay just over five minutes into the game and did not return, leaving punter Ethan Evans to attempt the crucial kick. The questionable call certainly helped Arizona. But the Rams had already given Brissett a free play and allowed a 21-yard completion on a drive that began with 47 seconds remaining and the Cardinals out of timeouts. Another questionable call, another loss Look, saying a team should have played better doesn't excuse a questionable call that helps decide the game. The officials still have a job to do, regardless of what happened before the flag. They're too talented to write off after six games. They're also 2-4, and the preseason hype isn't going to help them climb out of that hole. home.headline: Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams
home.blurb: TEMPE — The Arizona Cardinals are holding star rookie running back Jeremiyah Love out of practice on Wednesday as Week 6 preperations for the Los Angeles Rams ramp up. Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams Skip to main content SI.COM "Take him one day at a time. You know, we want to get this ankle right and do it the right way," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday. Love has been nursing an ankle injury through the opening stages of his rookie season after suffering a different ankle injury during preseason. While he hasn't missed any regular season action, Love's participation and impact has been slightly hindered. There's been some talks about potentially shutting Love down to allow the ankle to heal, though LaFleur didn't seem willing to do that. Arizona is just 1-4 and is again favored to lose in Los Angeles. "Listen, I'm going to try to be as candid as possible with also knowing that everyone's listening to this too, right? But he's a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. I mean, imagine being a running back in the NFL trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you know that you're capable of," LaFleur said. "And so we all are in agreeance — as much as you know he wants to battle through — we're all in agreeance right now, it's just hey, give [the injury] a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on, what that'll entail for Sunday." Love, the No. 3 overall pick, has 67 carries for 245 yards and one touchdown on the ground while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and a score through the air. "I think early at his career [he battled injuries], but you had the right [ankle] early, and then now you got the left one. So now you're just kind of — it's just double dipping. The right side, the preseason one's fine. It's the other one right now that's the lingering issue. They're ankles, you know, it's an ankle. I'm not a doctor, and each body's a little bit different," LaFleur continued. "Like the way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable, like he doesn't even feel it. But this one is the one that happened kind of when the regular season started, and it just lingered." Has Love lost any of his explosiveness? "You'd have to ask him that," LaFleur added. "I know how explosive he is. I know how explosive he wants to be. So I mean I think that's a fair assessment in some aspects. Again, I don't think it's an overall hindrance, but again the the rest for him is going to be vital." picks.blurb: Chiefs vs. Chargers: NFL Week 6 Preview, Score Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI For the third time in five games to begin the 2026-27 season, the Kansas City Chiefs will square off against an opponent from their own division. Coming out of the bye, it's the Los Angeles Chargers who stroll into Arrowhead Stadium to face Andy Reid's group. With Kansas City looking to maintain an undefeated record and Los Angeles' season hanging on by the thinnest of threads, many would assume that this has the makings of a blowout. Given how close these rivals usually play each other, though, is there the possibility of a more competitive Sunday showdown? How might today's game unfold? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 6 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: Undefeated vs. winless doesn’t really mean all that much to me once game day actually arrives. The Chiefs are coming off a bye, but they're still dealing with an array of impactful injuries . The Chargers are limping toward their week off, but it’s a divisional game. I don't expect the Chargers to magically find offensive success against the Chiefs, yet I could easily see this game being uglier than Chiefs fans would like. Jordan Foote: Kansas City is well rested for Week 6, and Reid's track record after a bye speaks for itself. Not only that, but the Chargers are struggling in two of the game's three phases (offense and special teams) and are extremely banged up to boot. This team is undoubtedly more talented than its record shows , which is why I'm calling for an ugly one-score game, but the hosts should be able to overcome their own injuries and rise to 5-0 on the still-young season. If the Chiefs lose this one, they have only themselves to blame. There's ample room for a hint of a nail-biter, albeit not an embarrassing loss to a floundering foe. Joshua Schulman: An undefeated Chiefs squad taking on a winless Chargers team feels like the biggest trap game of all time, but it’s hard to fathom just how bad Justin Herbert and Mike McDaniel's unit has been. While they’ve been trending up in recent weeks, poor late-game execution and costly turnovers have sunk their chances. Coming off a bye, I think the old “rest vs. rust” debate will play out for the Chiefs offense, and Patrick Mahomes may need some time to connect with his new targets now that Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton won’t be suiting up. However, they should come alive in the second half, and the defense will do enough to keep it close the first few quarters. Tyler Brown: Early in the week, this one felt closer than the records suggest. Chiefs-Chargers games have a history of being tight regardless of the circumstances, and that reputation is hard to shake. The longer the week went on, though, the harder it became to make a case for Los Angeles. This Chargers team is much closer to the Miami Dolphins the Chiefs dispatched 24-10 in Week 3 than they are to any legitimate AFC West contender. The injury report alone, with Joe Alt, Rashawn Slater, and Derwin James all out, makes this a mismatch. Add in the 0-5 record and four rookie offensive linemen protecting Herbert, and the case for a competitive game falls apart. The sack drought ends Sunday. Herbert has been sacked 30 times in 11 career games against Kansas City, and he's never faced this Chiefs defensive line with this little protection. Three to four sacks feels conservative, and one or two turnovers wouldn't be surprising. Walker should have another big day on the ground, and tight end Travis Kelce will get going without James lurking in the middle of the field. The young receivers will have a chance to build some chemistry with Mahomes in a low-stakes environment. away.headline: Kansas City Chiefs' first injury report for Week 6 tilt vs. Los Angeles Chargers shows a team on the mend after the bye week
away.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs have released their first injury report ahead of Week 6 against the Los Angeles Chargers. After having 10 players on the final injury report ahead of the Week 5 bye, Kansas City's roster appears to be on the mend. Rashee Rice didn't participate in practice on Wednesday, but the team removed 5 players who were hurt just two weeks ago from the injury report. For the first time since mid-August, Chiefs LT Josh Simmons took part in a limited practice session. Here’s a quick breakdown of each team's first Week 6 injury report. Keep in mind that clubs can add to the injury report through kickoff on Sunday. They will release game status designations on Friday, Oct. 16. KEY: DNP = Did not participate | LP = Limited participation | FP = Full participation | NIR = Not injury related As Coach Reid said, Rice did not participate, and Simmons participated in a limited capacity. Simmons moved gingerly in video taken during the open portion of practice ( see FOX 4's footage here ). The Kansas City Chiefs return from their earliest bye of the Patrick Mahomes era facing a 13-week stretch run. A thin wide receiver room and a few rising young players will change the rotation. away.headline: Ahead of Chiefs matchup, wounded, winless Chargers share lengthy injury report
away.blurb: Included in the list of injured players were starting left tackle Joe Alt (neck, DNP), star safety Derwin James Jr. (hamstring, DNP) and leading wide receivers Ladd McConkey (foot, limited participant) and Quentin Johnston (chest, limited). At wide receiver, Los Angeles is dealing with a plethora of issues. In addition to McConkey and Johnston’s ailments, Tre’ Harris (hamstring, DNP), Brenen Thompson (quadriceps, limited), and former Chief Marquez Valdes-Scantling (rib, limited) were listed on Wednesday’s report. Skip to content Best Deals KC KCTV Tower 3 Degree Guarantee MyKC Live It’s Your Health Advertise With Us Jobs KCTV5 Cares Choices, Hope, and Science Watch Live First Warn 5 Weather 7-Day Forecast Station Information Meet the Team KANSAS CITY, Mo. (KCTV) - A wounded and winless Los Angeles Chargers team is headed toward Kansas City this weekend looking to hand the Chiefs their first loss of the season. But those aforementioned wounds are mounting after five weeks of play, and Wednesday’s injury report shared by head coach Jim Harbaugh’s team was a lengthy one. In total, nearly 40 percent of the Chargers’ active roster were listed with some ailment after their first practice of the week. Not included on the injury report was Chargers center Tyler Biadasz, who was placed on season-ending injured reserve in August due to a torn ACL suffered in training camp and starting right tackle Rashawn Slater and backup Trey Pipkins, who were each placed on injured reserve in recent weeks due to ankle and knee issues. As a result, last week, injuries on the Chargers offensive line led to multiple rookies starting for Los Angeles in a game where star quarterback Justin Herbert was sacked five times. All of those injuries to Chargers pass-catchers, which include tight end David Njoku being placed on injured reserve in September, resulted in the Chargers hosting several wide receivers for tryouts on Tuesday and signing former Raymore-Peculiar and KU alum Luke Grimm to their practice squad. Kansas City and Los Angeles kick off Sunday’s game at 3:25 p.m. CT. It can be watched live in Kansas City and the surrounding viewing area on KCTV5.

They will release game status designations on Friday, Oct. 16. KEY: DNP = Did not participate | LP = Limited participation | FP = Full participation | NIR = Not injury related Chiefs rookie DT Peter Woods was added to the injury report with a neck injury after participating fully on Wednesday. His practice status on Friday will determine his availability for Sunday. However, the Raiders have surprised everyone and started the season 3-0. Their hot start has cooled down a bit, thanks to facing some heavy hitters in the conference. They lost their last two games, first falling to the Kansas City Chiefs ,30-27, in a hard-fought AFC West battle. Last week, they struggled against the defending AFC Champion New England Patriots , losing 45-17 and showing cracks in their unlikely season. The Bills can relate to Vegas' last loss, because Buffalo's only defeat this season came against their AFC East rival. Buffalo lost to the Patriots 29-26 in Week 4. Last week, the Bills squeaked out a win against the Los Angeles Rams in overtime, with a blocked kick saving the game for Buffalo. Bills vs. Raiders: need to know Ball security: The Bills do well in many categories, but turnovers have been an issue lately. Bills have nine turnovers in the last three games, with four coming from Josh Allen . Last week, running back James Cook had a crucial turnover in overtime, and while it worked out in the end, it did add to the turnover problem building on Buffalo's offense. The Bills' turnover differential is -4, and the Raiders' is +3. Offenses by the numbers: The Raiders' numbers are superior to the Bills' in the pass game, but Buffalo has them beat in the run game. The Raiders are seventh in the league in passing yards (1,317), while the Bills are 11th (1,249). Las Vegas is second in passing touchdowns (12), while the Bills are in the middle of the pack in the category (7). The Bills excel in rushing yards, ranking fourth in the NFL (790) and leading the NFL in rushing touchdowns (13). The Raiders have the fifth-fewest yards on the ground (410) and are toward the bottom in rushing touchdowns (2). Buffalo is tied for average points per game at 32.8. Defenses by the numbers: The Bills have the second-worst pass defense in the league in terms of yards allowed (1,479), while the Raiders are fourth-worst in rushing yards allowed (703). Raiders Maxx Crosby is tied for third-most quarterback pressures in the NFL (36) and Vegas' 10 takeaways are tied for most in the league. While Vegas got off to a solid start this season, I think their recent stretch is a bit too much for them to attack. I think the last two losses may be hard to shake off. I think the Bills will start to shake off their ball security problems and Allen just seems to be unstoppable, even when he is committing turnovers. I'm picking the Bills here, but I think the Raiders will have a good fight in them. One of the 10 without a game designation is starting right tackle Spencer Brown, who left the Week 5 win , and did not return, after 16 snaps due to a back flare-up. Brown practiced in a limited capacity on Wednesday before improving to full participation on Thursday and Friday. With a minor "muscle freak out" now in the rearview, the starting right tackle is ready for his 79th regular season appearance in a Bills' uniform. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The last time these two teams met in Week 4 of the 2025 season, they combined for the highest-scoring tie in the Super Bowl era Getty Images One of the NFL's highest-scoring rivalries will be renewed on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 6 when the Green Bay Packers (3-2) host the Dallas Cowboys (2-3) at Lambeau Field on Sunday night. Last season, the Packers traveled down to Texas to face the Cowboys at AT&T Stadium, and the two teams tied at 40-40, the highest-scoring tie in the Super Bowl era, since 1996, per CBS Sports Research. The game featured seven lead changes, including six consecutive touchdown drives with a lead change in the second half. However, this rivalry hasn't exactly been very competitive in terms of the games' final outcomes, with the Cowboys seeking their first win against the Packers since the 2016 regular season, quarterback Dak Prescott's rookie year. Since that game, Dallas is 0-5-1 in the last six games against Green Bay despite scoring 31 points per game in that stretch. The problem is their defense has allowed a combined 37 points per game during the six-game winless streak against the Packers. That's the most points per game scored by a team's offense during a six-game winless span against an opponent in NFL history, per CBS Sports Research. Sunday will mark Packers quarterback Jordan Love's first home start against the Cowboys, with both of his games against Dallas coming on the road -- a 48-32 wild card round win in the 2023 season and the 40-40 tie last year. It will also mark a homecoming for two former Packers who are now Cowboys: three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Kenny Clark and Pro Bowl edge rusher Rashan Gary . Let's dig into this primetime fight against two of the NFL's most historic franchises, but first, here's how you can watch: Where to watch Cowboys vs. Packers Date: Sunday, Oct. 18 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay, Wisconsin) TV: NBC | Stream: Fubo (try for free) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -1.5, O/U 53.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook) Cowboys vs. Packers need to know Cowboys looking to fix bad vibes on defense: In Week 5, Dallas lost a home game 24-16 on "Thursday Night Football" to the previously 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers , a team it was favored by 9.5 points. Tampa Bay was starting undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels , making his second career start in place of an injured Baker Mayfield , and Dallas allowed the Buccaneers to control the game with 241 rushing yards. That was the most for the Buccaneers in a game since the 2024 season. This week, there has been speculation from owner and general manager Jerry Jones about first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker moving upstairs to the booth, but Parker and head coach Brian Schottenheimer maintained he will remain on the sideline. Dallas' performance improvement plan has begun with the hiring of former Cleveland Browns coach Mike Pettine as a senior assistant . Pettine actually gave Parker his first job in the NFL when he was Green Bay's defensive coordinator in 2019. Dallas knows that being the league's 31st-ranked defense (395.4 total yards allowed per game), last-place run defense (168.4 rushing yards allowed per game), and worst third-down defense (52.6% third-down conversion rate allowed) won't cut it. How fixable are the issues? "Very fixable because they're under our control," Parker said. "Very fixable." Cowboys All-Pro defensive tackle Quinnen Williams agrees. "Just from the aspect of the things that we can control are the things that we're messing up on. Effort. Playing with our technique. Playing better, things like that. Those are things we can control as a unit, we can control as a unit. It's fixable. We just have to make our best effort to fix those things. Packers' Jordan Love aims to maintain an explosive passing game to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden : Packers quarterback Jordan Love is fresh off his best game of 2026 in Week 5, a 31-7 beatdown of the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field. Love completed 25 of his 31 throws for 367 yards and 2 touchdowns against Chicago, which makes him the Packers' record holder for the most passing yards in a game against the Bears at Lambeau Field. He beat the previous record of 345 yards passing by Lynn Dickey, set back in 1983. The victory, 24 points, ranks as the largest win against the Bears since 2014, the year Rodgers won the second of his four NFL MVPs. The Packers are now 5-3 against the Bears in Love's eight career starts against them since 2023, including playoffs. "We were flowing today. Executed at a really high level. I was proud of everybody. That's what it looks like when we play to our standard, and we got playmakers making plays down the field, O-line doing a great job," Love said postgame on FOX . "That's the standard for us. ... This is huge. This is a win we needed at home, getting us rolling and keep building off this." Love went big-game hunting with regularity to both wide receiver Christian Watson (143 yards receiving and 2 receiving touchdowns on 6 catches) and wide receiver Matthew Golden (123 yards receiving on 6 catches), making Watson and Golden the first Green Bay duo with 120-plus yards receiving in a game since 2016. It last occurred when Davante Adams and Jordy Nelson accomplished the feat against the Tennessee Titans 10 years ago. Love hit Watson for gains of 42 yards (the game's first touchdown that made the score 7-0), 31 yards and 53 yards (Love's second touchdown pass that made the score 20-7 with 13:10 left in the third quarter). LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. That's something that seems hard to bounce back from, because everyone looks dumb. Obviously, the buck stops with the head coach, but why did offensive coordinator David Blough call a play that USED MOTION as precious seconds ticked off the clock, and how was quarterbac

picks.blurb: Who Experts Are Picking For Dallas Cowboys vs. Green Bay Packers in Week 6 Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers enter their Week 6 contest at Lambeau Field on Sunday night coming off very different Week 5 showings. The Cowboys fell victim to the trap game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Dallas was heavily favored, and rightly so, as Tampa Bay was 0-4 and starting an undrafted rookie quarterback. But Dallas failed to so much as show up and fell to 2-3 on the year. The Packers, on the other hand, absolutely throttled the Chicago Bears in what was far and away Green Bay's best game on both sides of the ball. Now, all of the talk of the Packers' demise has been shelved. These two teams squared off last season and battled to a 40-40 tie. Before that, Green Bay had beaten Dallas in eight of their last nine meetings. Will the Packers continue their dominance over the Cowboys? Or will Dallas flip the script and pull out a win? Here's what experts from different media outlets think. The Packers defeated the Bears, 31-7. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Pete Prisco: Packers Jared Dubin: Packers Ryan Wilson: Packers John Breech: Cowboys Tyler Sullivan: Cowboys Dave Richard: Packers Jamey Eisenberg: Packers Pete Prisco: Packers Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) celebrates during the game between the Cowboys and the Buccaneers at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Jeremy Bergman: Packers Brooke Cersosimo: Packers Gennaro Filice: Packers Bobby Kownack: Cowboys Dan Parr: Packers Jeremy Bergman: Packers Final expert tally and my prediction Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer before the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Packers: 26 The biggest problem for the Cowboys in this game is Green Bay's ability to move the ball through the air . The Packers had struggled offensively over the first four contests, but they found their rhythm in Week 5 by torching the Bears with the deep ball. Defending the pass has been a major issue for the Cowboys this season, with Dallas ranking 21st. That doesn't even do justice for how bad it has really been. The Cowboys' ranking would be even worse if teams weren't abusing Christian Parker's unit on the ground. The good news for the Cowboys is the Packers haven't been able to run the football with any semblance of success, although Dallas presents a perfect get-right opportunity with their league-worst showing against the run this season. Green Bay has also struggled to stop the run, ranking 24th, but the Cowboys aren't running the ball like they did last season and it remains to be seen if they can capitalize on Green Bay's woes. Another problem for the Cowboys is the Packers are giving up the fifth-fewest yards per game through the air and if that holds true this week and the run game doesn't get on track, it's going to be tough sledding for Dallas' offense. Joey Porter Jr.'s return is going to make a dent in Dallas' passing game struggles, but the Cowboys still have the other side of the field to defend and DaRon Bland has proven incapable of doing that. The slot is a another concern if Caleb Downs is still playing most or all of his snaps at safety like he has amid the Cowboys' slew of injuries at safety. The Cowboys will get their points to keep this game close, but we're highly skeptical Dallas' secondary and pass-rush will do enough to keep Green Bay's passing attack at bay enough to emerge victorious. Final score prediction: Packers 30, Cowboys 27 Published Oct 16, 2026 MIKE MORAITIS Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. away.blurb: Turpin Cowboys injury clouds return game after opening kickoff hit Share Advertisement The Dallas Cowboys lost one of their most dangerous return threats before they had run an offensive snap against the Green Bay Packers. KaVontae Turpin was hurt on the opening kickoff Sunday night and was listed as questionable to return. The injury landed immediately in the spot where Turpin does his most damage. He is the Cowboys' primary return specialist, and the loss matters fast because the game had barely started when he was being walked to the locker room. Turpin's absence would be a real hit because he has become one of the most productive return men in football. He led the NFL in kickoff return yards in 2024, earned All-Pro honors for the first time that season and is a two-time Pro Bowler heading into his fifth season with the Cowboys. The team also has a fresh reason to watch his status closely after his three-year, $13.5 million extension in March 2025 and his July 2025 arrest on drug and weapons charges in Texas. For now, the immediate question is not whether the Cowboys can replace him for one play. It is whether they can keep the game from turning without the weapon that set their return unit apart before the night was even underway. Is Dj Moore Playing This Week? Last Thursday did not go as planned for Dallas, as the team suffered an embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at home, but the team gets an opportunity to bounce back in Week 6 with another primetime showdown. This weekend, Dallas will make the trip to Lambeau Field for a Sunday night showdown with the Green Bay Packers . But after some extra time to recover from the issues that left him throwing up in the locker room before being sent home , he is feeling well and on track to play on Sunday night. Porter was listed on Wednesday's report with an ankle issue, but it is not serious, and he will be in line for an increased workload this week. Per reports, Porter is expected to have a "near full workload" in Week 6 . Hopefully, everyone will continue improving as the week continues, with just two days remaining until game day. away.blurb: LG Aaron Banks (toe/knee): He practiced in a limited capacity all week, but it's his first week back from a multi-week injury. More than likely, the Packers will go with Laken Tomlinson at left guard against the Cowboys. Eventually, the Packers will have to make a long-term decision on their preferred starter at the position. DL Anthony Campbell (ankle) : His likely return from an ankle injury is coming at a good time considering the injury situation along the defensive front. It's possible Campbell will need to play double-digit snaps behind Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks and Chris McClellan on Sunday night. CB Brandon Cisse (hip): An unexpected addition to the injury report. Cisse injured his hip and was limited on Friday, creating the dreaded late-week injury and potential need to scramble for answers at a key position. Carrington Valentine would likely start if Cisse can't go. Depth at cornerback is under real stress ahead of matchup with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. WR Savion Williams (ankle): Is the second-year receiver ready to return from an ankle injury that had him on injured reserve to start the season? A natural replacement option for Skyy Moore, who is out, Williams could provide help as a gadget weapon on offense and in the return game if the Packers activate him to the 53-man roster before Sunday night. WR/KR Skyy Moore (ankle): The Packers' primary kick and punt returner injured his ankle last week and wasn't able to practice this week. It's possible the Packers will activate Savion Williams to help make up for Moore's absence in the return game and at receiver. The Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant and rookie offensive lineman Drew Shelton and listed linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, defensive lineman L.T Overton, cornerback Joey Porter Jr. and cornerback Ameer Speed as questionable on the final injury report. Receiver CeeDee Lamb (thigh) does not have an status designation and will play. How will the injury situation affect Sunday night's showdown with the Cowboys? Here’s an in-depth breakdown of the Packers ’ final injury report ahead of Week 6: OL Jacob Monk (quad): He's no longer a starting option at right guard, where Travis Glover or Kevin Zeitler will start Sunday, but Monk could be a backup at center and get snaps on special teams protection units if he's healthy. DL Jordon Riley (Achilles): He only just returned to practice this week, and even though the Packers need help along the defensive line, Riley is unlikely to play Sunday. He could be a factor as a run stuffer come next week or Week 8. DL Jonathan Ford (calf): His injury, combined with the season-ending injury to Javon Hargrave, puts the Packers in a tough place along the defensive front. Ford likely would have played a lot of snaps on Sunday if healthy. DL Javon Hargrave (Achilles): The veteran suffered a season-ending Achilles tendon injury last Sunday and will eventually go on injured reserve, possibly as soon as Saturday. CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring)

away.blurb: Cowboys Injury Report: 2 Out, 4 Questionable vs. Packers Home FRISCO, Texas — The Dallas Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant and offensive tackle Drew Shelton for Sunday night’s game at the Green Bay Packers , and listed linebacker DeMarvion Overshown , cornerback Joey Porter Jr. , defensive tackle L.T. Overton , and cornerback Ameer Speed as questionable on Friday’s final injury report. Durant and Shelton did not practice all week with hamstring injuries. Overshown was limited Thursday and Friday with his hamstring after missing Wednesday, and coach Brian Schottenheimer said Friday that he still considers Overshown a long shot. “Yeah, doing okay. Again, I still think it’s probably a long shot for this game, but it was good to see him out there moving around a little bit better,” Schottenheimer said. Porter appeared on the report with an ankle injury. He was limited Wednesday, a full participant Thursday, and limited again Friday. Porter missed last week’s loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with an illness, and defensive coordinator Christian Parker said Thursday that Porter’s workload would be heavily increased this week. Overton was added to the report Friday with a foot injury and did not practice. Speed was limited Thursday and Friday with a knee injury after missing Wednesday.
