home.blurb: When Will Josh Jacobs Play? Return Timeline for Packers RB After NFL Decision - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL When Will Josh Jacobs Play? Return Timeline for Packers RB After NFL Decision Josh Jacobs is nearing his return to the Green Bay Packers after missing the opening weeks of the 2026 NFL season. The veteran running back has been unavailable since the league placed him on the commissioner's exempt list in August while it reviewed his legal situation. The Packers have played without one of their leading offensive weapons throughout the opening stretch of the season. Jacobs will also miss Sunday night's game against the Dallas Cowboys, but there is now a clearer picture of when he could return. Josh Jacobs Is Eligible to Return Against the Lions Ayomide Adeduyite Mon, October 19, 2026 at 12:27 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs (8).Robert Goddin-Imagn Images Jacobs is expected to make his 2026 debut when the Green Bay Packers visit the Detroit Lions next Sunday. The NFL announced Friday that Jacobs would be removed from the commissioner's exempt list on Monday, making him eligible to practice and play again. The league placed Jacob on the list on Aug. 30 after he faced misdemeanor charges stemming from a May incident. He pleaded no contest to charges of battery and criminal damage to property in September. The NFL's investigation under its personal conduct policy remains ongoing. The league has not announced whether Jacobs will face additional discipline, although time spent on the exempt list may count toward a potential suspension. Packers' Offense Receives Its Starting Running Back Jacobs rushed for 929 yards and 13 touchdowns in 2025, his second season with the Packers after five years with the Las Vegas Raiders. His absence has forced Green Bay to rely on MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong Jr. in the backfield, with Chris Brooks sidelined by an ankle injury. The Packers are 3-2 entering Week 6 and sit third in the NFC North behind the Minnesota Vikings (5-0) and Chicago Bears (4-2). home.headline: Green Bay Packers: NFL insider reveals the new Micah Parsons return target
home.blurb: Hopefully, Green Bay can avoid any more serious injuries. On the positive side, they are expecting to get two key contributors back very soon. It has recently been reported that Pro Bowl running back Josh Jacobs will return as the starting running back in Week Seven. Additionally, All-Pro pass rusher Micah Parsons is getting closer and closer to his own return. NFL insider expects Micah Parsons to return in Week 9 for the Green Bay Packers Initially, many hoped that the All-Pro pass rusher would be able to return for Green Bay’s Week Six matchup against his former team. However, the Packers have not opened up his practice window as they want to ensure that he is 100% healthy and not at risk for any soft tissue injuries because of rushing a return to the field. “A league source tells me Parsons might not return until Week 9, against the Patriots on Nov. 8. The Packers did not open his practice window this week to begin his return. In Week 7, Green Bay plays the Detroit Lions before hosting the Panthers on “’Thursday Night Football’; believing Parsons needs more than a week to ramp up, the short-week turnaround would be difficult to pull off.” If this is truly the targeted return date, it would be realistic to see Parsons designated for return by Green Bay this week. This means he would be able to practice with the rest of the team, and the Packers would have 21 days to add him to the active roster. While he will not play in that many games in 2026, Green Bay is hopeful that his return will take their already impressive defense under Jonathan Gannon to an even higher level. The Green Bay Packers have lost several players to season-ending injuries already this year. These include defensive stars Edgerrin Cooper and Javon Hargrave as well as offensive stars Zach Tom and Jayden Reed. Despite these losses, and terrible play from their offensive line early in year, Green Bay has gone 3-2 in their first five games. Parsons, who was acquired prior to the start of the 2025 season in a trade with the Dallas Cowboys, tore his ACL in late in the year and has missed every game of 2026 thus far. Jonathan Jones of The Athletic reported on Saturday morning that those around the NFL expect Parsons back in Week Nine when Green Bay faces the New England Patriots : Last season, Parsons became the first player in NFL history to record 12+ sacks in each of his first five seasons. He had 12.5 in 14 games played in his first season with the Packers and was named First Team All-Pro. San Francisco enters the Week 6 matchup at 5-0 after an exciting 32-29 road victory over the Seattle Seahawks, while Washington arrives at 1-3-1 following a frustrating 27-27 overtime tie against the New York Giants. The matchup presents two teams heading in different directions. The 49ers have found ways to win close games, while the Commanders are searching for consistency as they attempt to climb back into the NFC playoff conversation. Kickoff is scheduled for 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN and ABC. Brock Purdy Leads San Francisco's Offense Quarterback Brock Purdy has helped guide the 49ers through an impressive opening stretch. Although San Francisco has faced several challenging opponents, the offense has continued producing at important moments. Purdy threw two touchdown passes against Seattle and helped lead the game-winning drive that set up Eddy Piñeiro's decisive field goal. His ability to distribute the football and make smart decisions has been important to the team's success. Running back Christian McCaffrey remains another major weapon. His versatility as both a runner and receiver gives head coach Kyle Shanahan several ways to attack opposing defenses. San Francisco will look to establish its running game early, create favorable passing situations and control the tempo. The 49ers' offense has also benefited from contributions across the roster, allowing the team to remain productive even when individual drives become difficult. Jayden Daniels Looks to Spark Washington Washington will rely on quarterback Jayden Daniels to help generate offense against a San Francisco defense that has started the season strongly. Daniels demonstrated his playmaking ability against the Giants, rushing for 103 yards and two touchdowns while throwing for 199 yards. However, Washington's inability to finish the game left the team with a disappointing tie. Daniels' mobility could be one of the Commanders' biggest advantages. San Francisco will need disciplined defensive play to prevent him from escaping the pocket and creating explosive gains with his legs. Washington also needs better protection up front and more consistent execution on third downs. Sustaining drives will be particularly important against a 49ers team that has repeatedly capitalized on scoring opportunities. Kyle Shanahan vs. Dan Quinn The coaching matchup adds another layer to Monday night's game. Shanahan has San Francisco playing confident football, while Quinn needs Washington to respond after letting a potential victory slip away. For the Commanders, limiting turnovers and improving their second-half execution will be essential. The 49ers, meanwhile, will look to continue their balanced offensive approach and use their home-field advantage. A Major Test for Both Teams San Francisco has an opportunity to improve to 6-0 and strengthen its position in the NFC West.
